title: Misc. bug: Performance regression: CUDA sparse flash attention decode 1.6x slower (b11047 -> b11062)
body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11062, commit 3cf03257f)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Compared against build 11047, commit `b23701f77`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

ggml (CUDA backend)

### Command line

```bash
test-backend-ops perf -b CUDA0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT
```

Built with:

```
-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_CUDA_FA=ON -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON -DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`FLASH_ATTN_EXT` on the sparse path costs 64 percent more at batch one after
[#28770](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28770), median over the 11 sparse configurations
`test-backend-ops` generates. The worst is 113 percent. Dense shapes are untouched. RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell
Workstation Edition, sm_120, driver 615.71.09, CUDA 13.4.

Run the command above at `3cf03257f` and at `b23701f77` and compare the configurations whose `n_kv_max` is not 0.
Use console output, since `--output csv` drops the timings.

Every sparse configuration, `us/run`:

| hsk | nh  | kv    | n_kv_max | b11047 | b11062 | delta |
| --- | --- | ----- | -------- | ------ | ------ | ----- |
| 512 | 1   | 49152 | 2048     | 25.80  | 55.01  | +113% |
| 512 | 1   | 32768 | 512      | 18.29  | 37.58  | +106% |
| 576 | 1   | 49152 | 2048     | 29.17  | 58.83  | +102% |
| 576 | 1   | 32768 | 512      | 21.78  | 41.60  | +91%  |
| 512 | 1   | 16384 | 512      | 13.58  | 23.27  | +71%  |
| 256 | 2   | 32768 | 2048     | 22.55  | 36.97  | +64%  |
| 576 | 1   | 16384 | 512      | 17.12  | 27.14  | +59%  |
| 256 | 2   | 16384 | 2048     | 15.03  | 22.53  | +50%  |
| 512 | 1   | 4096  | 512      | 10.21  | 12.64  | +24%  |
| 576 | 1   | 4096  | 512      | 13.59  | 16.18  | +19%  |
| 256 | 2   | 4096  | 2048     | 16.45  | 11.81  | -28%  |

Dense shapes over the same range moved 0.1 percent median on 58 decode configurations and 0.3 percent on 29 batched
ones. Nothing outside the sparse path changed.

**Where the time goes.** Dividing the added time by the mask width gives a constant, within each head size and across
a twelve-fold range of `kv`:

| hsk | nh  | kv    | n_kv_max | added us | ns per mask column |
| --- | --- | ----- | -------- | -------- | ------------------ |
| 512 | 1   | 4096  | 512      | +2.43    | 0.593              |
| 512 | 1   | 16384 | 512      | +9.69    | 0.591              |
| 512 | 1   | 32768 | 512      | +19.29   | 0.589              |
| 512 | 1   | 49152 | 2048     | +29.21   | 0.594              |
| 576 | 1   | 4096  | 512      | +2.59    | 0.632              |
| 576 | 1   | 16384 | 512      | +10.02   | 0.612              |
| 576 | 1   | 32768 | 512      | +19.82   | 0.605              |
| 576 | 1   | 49152 | 2048     | +29.66   | 0.603              |

The cost tracks `kv` and ignores `n_kv_max`, including across the pair at `n_kv_max` 512 and 2048 that read 0.589 and
0.594. The attention kernel's work is bounded by `n_kv_max`, so it cannot produce this. The mask scan reads exactly
`kv` columns per list, so it can. I have not profiled the two kernels separately, so this is inference from the
scaling rather than a direct attribution.

It points at the new inner loop in `flash_attn_mask_to_sparse_indices`:

```c
for (int q = 0; q < q1 - q0 && !selected; ++q) {
    selected = i < ne30 && isfinite(__half2float(mask[q*s31 + i]));
}
```

where it used to be a single test. The trip count is a runtime value and the exit is data dependent, so the
`#pragma unroll` over `values_per_lane` around it no longer yields straight line code. At `ncols1 == 1` the body
always runs once and the union reduces to the old single-query test, so specialising that case, or templating the
kernel on `ncols1`, would recover it without touching the batched path the PR was written for.

The one configuration that improved, `kv=4096` at `n_kv_max=2048`, fits the same reading. The new per-list count
bounding `kb0_stop` is a real win, and at that shape it is larger than the scan cost.

**Scope.** `test-backend-ops` only generates sparse configurations at `nb=1`, so this says nothing about the batched
sparse path. The models reaching it are the ones calling `ggml_flash_attn_ext_set_n_kv_max`, currently `qwen4exp` and
`deepseek4`. A server decoding at batch one, meaning one slot and no draft model, sits on the regressed shape for
every token.

### First Bad Commit

`3cf03257f` (#28770, "CUDA: enable sparse fa for qwen4").

15 commits separate `b23701f77` from `3cf03257f`, and only `3cf03257f` touches `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/` at all. The rest
are Metal, Hexagon, server, chat and UI changes.

I measured [#28536](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28536) separately, as the other CUDA flash attention
change in the neighbourhood. It costs 0.7 percent on these same configurations, so it is not involved.

title: Eval bug: qwen4exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) on Metal: decode emits 1 token then EOS at long context — silent empty output, stochastic at threshold, threshold moves with model quant / KV quant / n_ctx
body:
### Name and Version
0.3.0-dev (build 37, commit 8e53fce), built with AppleClang 21.0.0 for Darwin arm64 (Metal, default flags, Release)

### Operating systems
Mac

### GGML backends
Metal

### Hardware
2x Apple M1 Max (24-core and 32-core GPU), 64 GB unified memory each — reproduced on both

### Models
- unsloth-style AD-3.84bpw-IQ4_XS-M64 (28 shards) — 16K/64K OK, 128K FAIL
- AD-4.27bpw-Q4_K_M-M64 (33 shards) — 64K FAIL (q4v4 KV) / 16K FAIL (q8v8 KV)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce
llama-server, single slot, GPU flash attention (auto). With prompts beyond a config-dependent threshold:
- prefill completes normally (e.g. 118-140 tok/s at 64K)
- decode emits exactly 1 token then stops (EOS): `eval time = ... / 1 tokens`, answer empty
- server returns HTTP 200 — silent failure, no error anywhere
- at/near the threshold the failure is STOCHASTIC: same server, same config, same prompt size → 64K x3 = PASS, PASS, FAIL on consecutive runs
- threshold moves with model quant (Q4_K_M << IQ4_XS), KV quant (q8v8+b256: 16K vs q4v4+b512: 64K), and possibly n_ctx window size (64K probes 3/3 @ n_ctx 208896 vs 2/3 @ n_ctx 262144, same 64K prompts)
- with mixed-precision KV (-ctk q8_0 -ctv q4_0) Metal rejects FA → attention falls back to CPU → 200K needle tests pass 3/3 (correct but slow) — so the failure is specific to the GPU attention path
- `-fa off` cannot be tested with quantized KV ("quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled"); with f16 KV + `-fa off` decode fails immediately with `Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 256, ret = -3` on the first token
- memory pressure excluded (failures observed with < 600 MB swap)
- needle-in-haystack probe (3 pins at 10/50/90% depth), warmup, temperature 0

Matrix (all llama-server, GPU FA, IQ4_XS unless noted):
| model | KV | -b/-ub | n_ctx | 16K | 64K | 128K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IQ4_XS | q4v4 | 512 | 208896 | 3/3 | 3/3,3/3,3/3 | 0/3 (1 tok) |
| IQ4_XS | q4v4 | 1024 | 208896 (A machine, +ngram spec) | — | 3/3 (32K/64K) | 0/3 (1 tok) |
| IQ4_XS | q8v8 | 1024 | 262144 | — | 3/3,3/3,0/3 (stochastic!) | not reached |
| Q4_K_M | q4v4 | 512 | 208896 | — | 0/3 | — |
| Q4_K_M | q8v8 | 256 | 208896 | 0/3 | — | — |

### First Bad Commit
Unknown; qwen4exp support landed via #27742 (2026-08-27) — all failures observed on builds containing it. **Retested on master `df03399` (0.4.0-dev build 300, contains #27941, #28023, #28098): the bug reproduces identically.** 64K x1 = 3/3 (prefill 153.8 tok/s, decode 11.1 — sparse-FA perf improvements visible), 128K x1 = **0/3, decode 0.0 (1 tok)** — same signature, same threshold. So #27941 (block position keying), #28023 (indexer head summation) and Metal sparse FA do not resolve it.

### Related
#27856 (HIP: depth-decay only, output correct), #28734 (CUDA: dense top-k TODO), #25722 (Metal: degenerate-token silent empty output, different arch), #21450 (Metal mixed KV rejection — the mechanism that pushes attention to CPU and avoids this bug)

*Disclosure: issue text prepared with AI assistance (GLM-5.3-Flash via ZCode), verified against server logs and raw probe JSONs.*

title: Misc. bug: /slots save/restore never persists the draft-model context (ctx_dft) on speculative-decoding deployments
body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.3.0-dev (build 1, commit 0f3a71b)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Reproduced against `ggml-org/llama.cpp` commit `0f3a71be15af836d277c9f918adfafb45732677e`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --parallel 1 \
  -c 262144 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -fa on \
  --slot-save-path /slot-cache
```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=save|restore` only persists `ctx_tgt` (via
`llama_state_seq_save_file`/`llama_state_seq_load_file`) — on a deployment
running speculative decoding (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`), the draft
model's own context (`ctx_dft`) is never captured or restored at all.

This is a separate, narrower gap from #25913 (checkpoints not persisted,
addressed by #26004): even once #26004 lands, a restored slot's draft
model only gets its state back if a checkpoint happened to already exist
at save time (checkpoints carry their own `data_dft`) — a short
conversation that hasn't hit its first checkpoint yet restores with an
empty draft-model KV cache and no fallback. The raw, currently-live
`ctx_dft` state is simply discarded on save, independent of checkpoint
existence.

Not directly observable as a crash or an error — the restore reports
success either way — but on a speculative-decoding deployment it means
the draft model silently starts cold after every restore whenever no
checkpoint happens to cover the request, undermining part of the benefit
`--slot-save-path` is meant to provide alongside #26004's fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start `llama-server` with a draft model (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`)
   and `--slot-save-path`.
2. Send a short prompt (short enough that it completes before the first
   context checkpoint would be created) with `cache_prompt: true`.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`.
4. Inspect the save file: only the `ctx_tgt` payload
   (`llama_state_seq_save_file`'s own format) is present; there is no
   companion draft-model state anywhere.
5. `POST /slots/0?action=erase`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
6. The restore succeeds and reports the correct token count, but
   `ctx_dft` was never touched — the draft model's KV cache is empty,
   identical to a slot that just came up cold, regardless of what #26004
   restores for `ctx_tgt`/checkpoints.

### First bad commit

Not a regression — `SLOT_SAVE`/`SLOT_RESTORE` have never captured
`ctx_dft`; this predates both this report and #26004.

### Relationship to other issues/PRs

- #25913 / #26004: separate root cause (missing checkpoint persistence
  for `ctx_tgt`'s reuse-validity check), already well covered there. This
  report is about `ctx_dft` specifically, which #26004 does not touch.
- We have a working fix (raw `ctx_dft` capture/restore via
  `llama_state_seq_get_size_ext`/`get_data_ext`/`set_data_ext`, stored as
  a companion `<save-file>.dft`, verified live on a production
  Vulkan/AMD-APU draft-mtp deployment) and are happy to open it as a PR,
  either standalone or as a follow-up once #26004 merges (to avoid
  competing for review attention on the same file/handlers at once) —
  see our comment on #26004 for details.

title: ggml_gallocr silently reuses stale allocation plan on identity change at fixed position (sparse MoE corruption)
body:
### Summary

`ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()` reuses a stale allocation plan when a node at the **same graph position** changes **identity** but not size — silent memory corruption on repeated `ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph()` calls with dynamic-topology graphs (sparse MoE routing).

### File / functions

`ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c` — `ggml_gallocr_node_needs_realloc` (~line 997), `ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc` (~line 1009), `ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph` (~line 1052).

### Root cause

```c
static bool ggml_gallocr_node_needs_realloc(ggml_gallocr_t galloc, struct ggml_tensor * node, struct tensor_alloc * talloc) {
    size_t node_size = 0;
    if (!node->data && !node->view_src) {
        if (talloc->buffer_id < 0) {
            return false;
        }
        node_size = ggml_backend_buft_get_alloc_size(galloc->bufts[talloc->buffer_id], node);
    }
    return talloc->size_max >= node_size;   // <-- SIZE ONLY, no identity/op/shape comparison
}
```

`ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()` calls this once per node and once per non-NULL `src[j]`, indexed purely by **position** `i` in `graph->nodes[]` — it never checks that `graph->nodes[i]` is the same logical tensor as when the plan for that position was built, only that node/leaf counts and per-position byte size still fit.

If a backend's scheduler (or any dynamic-topology graph builder — sparse MoE routing is the clearest trigger) produces two graphs where position `i` holds two *different* tensors that happen to have a compatible size, `ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc()` returns `false`, the stale offset table is silently reused, and the new tensor is written into memory reserved for the old one — **no error, no assertion, no warning** at any log level.

This is distinct from the already-fixed ggml-org/ggml#999 ("gallocr: fix reallocation of shared tensors", closed 2024-10-31), which addressed conflicting allocations for tensors *shared between graphs*. This is about a single graph position silently changing identity between successive calls on the *same* `ggml_gallocr_t` — a different code path, still present.

### Reproduction (real hardware, two independent cases)

Qualcomm Hexagon NPU backend (`ggml-hexagon`), OnePlus 15 / Snapdragon SM8850, batch-1 decode of sparse-MoE models. A local diagnostic patch (not upstream — hashes node op+name+shape into a signature and compares it in addition to the stock size-only check) demonstrates exactly which invariant fails:

**1. `gemma-4-26B-A4B.Q2_K.gguf`** (Gemma4 MoE), reproduced both HTP-offloaded **and CPU-only** (`-ngl 0`), ruling out anything NPU-specific:

```
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc: DIAGNOSTIC plan/identity mismatch at node 2639 (result_norm):
plan signature 618212584c166e89, current de842b29e5861e97
(counts/sizes matched, but tensor at this position differs from the one the plan was built for
— possible silent corruption if plan is reused)
```

**2. `Marco-Nano-Instruct.Q4_0.gguf`** (Qwen3-MoE, 256 experts/8 active), separate build/commit:

```
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc: DIAGNOSTIC plan/identity mismatch at node 1876 (ffn_moe_weighted-27 (view)): ...
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc: DIAGNOSTIC plan/identity mismatch at node 1892 (result_norm): ...
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc: DIAGNOSTIC plan/identity mismatch at node 1893 (result_output): ...
```

Same pattern on a different model/build — general MoE / dynamic-topology issue in the allocator's reuse check, not model- or build-specific.

Observed symptom in both cases at the application level: **silently corrupted output** (grammatically-shaped but semantically incoherent text / garbage tokens), no crash, no error at default log level.

### Suggested fix

Compare a cheap identity signature (e.g. `node->op`, `node->name`/interned id, shape) in addition to size in `ggml_gallocr_node_needs_realloc()`. If it differs from what was recorded when the plan for that position was built, force a realloc for that node (ideally just that node, to avoid regressing the fast-path the plan cache exists for).

### Why this likely hasn't surfaced widely

Requires (a) reusing the same `ggml_gallocr_t` across many calls — standard for decode loops — and (b) runtime-dependent graph topology at fixed node/leaf count, which is rare outside sparse-MoE routing or custom schedulers that reorder nodes non-canonically between calls. Dense models essentially never trigger it since their graph shape is static token-to-token.

### Environment

- Device: OnePlus 15 (Snapdragon SM8850), Android
- Backend: `ggml-hexagon` fork (HTP0), reproduced both HTP-offload and CPU-only
- Models: `gemma-4-26B-A4B.Q2_K.gguf` (Gemma4 MoE), `Marco-Nano-Instruct.Q4_0.gguf` (Qwen3-MoE)

🤖 Report compiled with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: CUDA: make GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON the default (silent CPU fallback for 4-bit KV)
body:
Building with the default flags, using a 4-bit KV cache (q4_0/q4_1) silently drops prefill to CPU speed. No warning, no offload message, just a ~30x slowdown that is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

What happens: the kernel selection in fattn.cu (ggml_cuda_fattn_kv_type_supported) only accepts f16/f32 KV unless GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS is set at compile time. When the requested KV type is not supported, the scheduler places the whole FLASH_ATTN_EXT op on the CPU backend.

Measured on a single RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-27B, K=q4_1 / V=q8_0, 130K ctx:

| build | prefill |
|---|---|
| default | ~34 t/s |
| -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON | 659-1094 t/s depending on context |

This is the third report of the same silent fallback in #27109 (myself, @aand18, @Cybertiron). Every user who wants 4-bit KV to fit long contexts in limited VRAM has to discover this flag on their own, and release builds ship without it.

Ask: make GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON the default in the CMake option, or at minimum print a clear warning at startup when the requested KV cache types cannot be served by the CUDA FA kernel.

PR #28634 flips the default.

title: Misc. bug: (OpenAI compat) unsupported "dimensions" parameter in embeddings endpoint
body:
### Name and Version llama-cli --version version: 9859 (4fc4ec554) built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64 ### Operating systems Windows, Linux, Mac, BSD ### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected? llama-server ### Command line ```shell # model pre-downloaded from HuggingFace: unsloth/embeddinggemma-300m-GGUF llama-server --embedding --model models/embeddinggemma-300m/embeddinggemma-300M-BF16.gguf --alias embeddinggemma-300m --ctx-size 2048 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 ``` ### Problem description & steps to reproduce According to [OpenAI API, /v1/embeddings](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/embeddings/methods/create) endpoint accepts optional `dimensions` parameter to specify desired embedding vector dimensions amount in the server response. Llama.cpp doesn't support this parameter.
Example request/response Request (POST `/v1/embeddings`): ```jsonc { "input": "Hello world", "dimensions": 128 // desired dimensions: 128 } ``` Response (llama.cpp): ```jsonc { "model": "embeddinggemma-300m", "object": "list", "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 4, "total_tokens": 4 }, "data": [ { "embedding": [... 768 numbers ...], // returned: 768 (model embedding length), expected: 128 (model supports MRL) "index": 0, "object": "embedding" } ] } ```
--- There are many embedding models which supports different embedding dimensionality using, for example, MRL approach (Matryoshka Representational Learning, [arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.13147), [sbert.net / sentence_transformer](https://sbert.net/examples/sentence_transformer/training/matryoshka/README.html)), for example: * OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` and `small` * Nomic `nomic-embed-text-v1.5` * Jina AI `jina-embeddings-v3`, `v4` and `v5` * Mixedbread `mxbai-embed-large-v1` * Google `embeddinggemma-300b` * Snowflake `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5` As a potential solution you can refer to the #24898 Pull request. ### First Bad Commit _No response_ ### Relevant log output _No response_

title: Feature Request: Fast Tool Gating & Single-Pass Selection via Prefill Logit Slicing
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

## Motivation
In modern agentic workflows (e.g., ReAct, function calling, tool use), models spend significant wall-clock time autoregressively generating tokens just to make discrete routing decisions (e.g., spelling out `<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_weather"...}`).

## What is the proposed solution
A special agent mode to fasten tool calls through "Jev-like" hybrid mode

Currently, when tools are provided in `llama-server` or `llama-cli`:
1. The engine prefills the prompt.
2. It enters the autoregressive decode loop ($O(N)$ sequential token passes) using either GBNF grammar constraints or hoping the chat template emits tool tokens correctly.
3. If the model chooses *not* to call a tool, or chooses a simple tool, we still pay the latency penalty of sequential token decoding and grammar state-machine transitions before knowing the routing outcome.

Because the prompt prefill pass **already computes the full KV cache and logits for the final prompt token**, we can resolve binary tool-gating decisions and tool-name enums in **$O(1)$ single forward passes** via logit slicing, falling back seamlessly to standard text generation without wasting the prefilled KV cache.

---

## Proposed Architectural Flow

```
[Prompt + Registered Tools] 
          │
          ▼
   llama_decode() (Prefill)
          │
          ▼
Inspect logits of last token: P(Tool Call) vs P(Chat/Text)
          │
   ┌──────┴────────────────────────────────┐
   ▼                                       ▼
P(Chat) > Threshold               P(Tool) > Threshold
   │                                       │
   │ (Zero KV cache waste)                 ▼
   │ Direct stream to user        Slice logits over registered 
   │ (Standard Autoregressive)    tool names: P(tool_1...tool_N)
                                           │
                                  ┌────────┴─────────────────┐
                                  ▼                          ▼
                         Bounded Enums/Booleans     Unbounded String Args
                         (Parallel Logit Slices)    (Switch to GBNF / AR loop)
```

### 1. Zero-Cost Gating Check (Prefill Inspection)
Right after `llama_decode()` on the prompt batch, before initializing the autoregressive decode loop:
* Inspect the logits of the final sequence position (`llama_get_logits_ith(ctx, -1)`).
* Measure the probability mass of the model's tool delimiter token (e.g., `<tool_call>`, `[TOOL]`, or `{` depending on the active Jinja chat template) against normal text tokens.
* **If text generation is chosen:** Continue the decode loop immediately. The KV cache is already fully initialized; overhead is virtually $0$ ms.

### 2. $O(1)$ Discrete Tool Selection
If the model indicates a tool call:
* Instead of sequentially generating the tool name string (e.g., `"name": "get_weather_data"` across multiple decode steps), the engine can mask the logits over the first tokens of the user-registered tools:
  $$\text{Softmax}\left(\text{logits}[\text{id}(\text{tool}_1), \text{id}(\text{tool}_2), \dots]\right)$$
* Select the candidate with highest calibrated confidence in a single step.

### 3. Argument Resolution Split
* **Bounded arguments (Enums, Booleans):** Handled via single-pass logit slicing.
* **Unbounded arguments (Raw strings, free text):** Switch back to standard autoregressive generation, with GBNF constrained only to that specific string argument.

---

## Key Benefits
1. **Dramatic Latency Reduction in Agent Loops:** Eliminates 10–50 sequential autoregressive steps for routing decisions, reducing decision latency to the prefill time (~15–40 ms on modern hardware).
2. **Zero Wasted Computation on Fallback:** Because the prompt prefill already took place, falling back to standard conversational text streaming incurs zero recomputation or KV-cache invalidation.
3. **No Syntax Failures for Tool Routing:** Eliminates malformed tool name keys and invalid enum tool selections at the root.

---



## Alternatives Considered
* **Full GBNF Grammar Decoding:** Guarantees syntax correctness, but incurs full sequential decode latency ($O(N)$ forward passes) even for basic if/else decisions.
* **Draft Model Speculative Decoding:** Requires loading a second model into VRAM and doesn't solve the structural inefficiency of using autoregression for discrete enum selection.


### Motivation

Save a lot of inference and compute when performing tool calls

### Possible Implementation


1. **`llama-server` (`/v1/chat/completions`):**
   * Introduce an optional flag, e.g., `--speculative-tool-gating` or a request parameter `"tool_choice": "auto_fast"`.
   * If enabled, check the top-K logits of the prefill output against the model's configured tool-call trigger tokens before attaching the full GBNF grammar parser.
2. **C API (`llama.h`):**
   * Expose a helper utility or sampler stage:
     ```c
     // Evaluates probabilities exclusively across a masked subset of candidate tokens
     // on the current prefilled context position without advancing the decode sequence.
     LLAMA_API void llama_sample_token_distribution(
         struct llama_context * ctx,
         const llama_token    * candidate_tokens,
         size_t                 n_candidates,
         float                * out_probs
     );
     ```

### Edge Case: Multi-Token Tool Names & Shared Prefixes

To handle tools that share initial tokens (e.g., `get_weather` vs `get_stock`):

1. **Trie-Based Logit Slicing:** Construct a Token Trie of registered tools. Non-branching prefixes are auto-advanced, and logit slicing only triggers at branching nodes (reducing steps from full JSON generation to Trie depth $D \le 2$).
2. **Batched Sequence Evaluation:** Alternatively, fork the existing context KV-cache across candidate tool sequences in a single batched `llama_decode()` pass to score cumulative log-probabilities in $O(1)$ time. (seems MTP/DFlash friendly to me)
3. **Index Token Aliasing:** In `llama-server`, map tools to discrete index tokens `[A, B, C]` within the tool definition template to ensure candidate IDs are always strictly 1 token.

title: Feature Request: export/import slots over http
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Add new routes to export/import a slot over the http api.

### Motivation

A proxy like https://github.com/kokleong98/llama-proxy-cache or https://gitlab.com/inqode/ai-proxy that sits in front of multiple llama.cpp instances can route requests to different llama.cpp instances.

If requests from a longer session are routed to different backends on each request, the KV cache of each instance can not be used effectively. Multiple llama.cpp instances will occupy slots for the same session (could probably be mitigated by using "/slots/{slot}?action=save|restore" - but would require disk write/read on the inference machine). Also on each switch of a session from one backend to another, parts of the KV will have to be recomputed.

### Possible Implementation

Add two routes: `GET /slots/{SLOT}/state` and `PUT /slots/{SLOT}/state`.

These routes could use the same binary format that `POST /slots/{SLOT}?action=save` and `POST /slots/{SLOT}?action=load` are using to persist a slot to disk.

- `GET /slots/{SLOT}/state` will return a stream of the slot state
- `PUT /slots/{SLOT}/state` will accept a stream of the slot state

title: tool_choice "required" is advisory, not grammar-enforced (Qwen3, --jinja); a warm KV-cache prefix reliably flips the same near-tie
body:
## What happens

`tool_choice: "required"` is not enforced by a grammar on this build: at `temperature: 0.7` with `cache_prompt: false` (so no cache is involved at all, `cached_tokens: 0` on every request), 2 of 10 otherwise-identical requests still answered in plain text with `tool_calls: []` instead of calling the tool, purely from sampling variance. A warm slot KV-cache prefix pushes that same near-tie the wrong way deterministically even at `temperature: 0`: llama-server returns the tool call on the first request, then answers in plain text with `tool_calls: []` on later requests whose prefix the slot's KV cache already holds. `cache_prompt: false` makes every request at `temperature: 0` honour the choice. `--cache-reuse 0` changes nothing.

## Build and model

- llama-server b10797, macOS arm64 (Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB, macOS 26.x)
- Qwen3-8B, Q4_K_M GGUF, the model's own chat template through `--jinja`
- Flags: `-c 32768 --parallel 1 -fa on -ngl all --reasoning off -ub 1024 --jinja --cache-reuse 256 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --metrics`

## Request (identical every time)

```json
{
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "who is the president of chile"}],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "websearch",
    "description": "Search the web.",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "required": ["expression"],
      "properties": {"expression": {"type": "string"},
                     "category": {"type": "string", "enum": ["images"]},
                     "read_page": {"type": "boolean"}}}}}],
  "tool_choice": "required",
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
  "max_tokens": 64, "temperature": 0, "cache_prompt": true
}
```

## Observed

| Set | Shape | Tool calls returned |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | identical request x5, `cache_prompt: false` | 5/5 (`usage.cached_tokens` 0) |
| A2 | identical request x5, `cache_prompt: true`, cache warm | 0/5 (`cached_tokens` 197 of 198; content "The current president of Chile is ...") |
| A3 | five requests differing only in the country, `cache_prompt: true` | 2/5 (peru, norway called the tool; chile, kenya, japan answered in text; all reused the prefix, 187 or 197 cached tokens) |
| A4 | fresh server with `--cache-reuse 0`, A2 again | 1/5 (the first request on the empty cache called the tool, the next four answered in text) |

Server log on every full-hit failure:

```
W slot   operator(): id  0 | task 185 | need to evaluate at least 1 token for each active slot (n_past = 198, task.n_tokens() = 198)
W slot   operator(): id  0 | task 185 | n_past was set to 197
```

The partial-reuse failures in A3 log no warning: ten or eleven new tokens are evaluated, then the reply is plain text.

## Expected

`tool_choice: "required"` returns a tool call on every request, whatever the slot's cache state; the OpenAI semantics do not depend on prompt caching.

## Open question for the maintainers

Is `required` enforced by a (non-lazy) grammar for the Qwen3 / Hermes-style template on this build, or only by the template's prompt? A grammar-enforced choice could not produce plain content in A2. If it is a grammar, the cache path appears to skip it; if it is not, the cache only changes which side of a near-tie the deterministic sampling lands on, and `required` is advisory. Happy to run either check.

title: Misc. bug: ggml-rpc-server crashes on vulkan when a duplicate copy of libggml-vulkan is dlopened
body:
### Name and Version

$ llama-server --version
version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11051, commit 5b59b83f4)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

Other (Please specify in the next section)

### Command line

```shell
ggml-rpc-server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 50052 -c
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Starting the RPC server results in an immediate crash.

Since f172be756 ("vulkan: split buffers and debug code into separate files, add shared headers", #28732) the Vulkan backend's internal cross-TU symbols (`vk_instance`, `ggml_vk_init`, `ggml_vk_instance_init`, ...) are exported from  `libggml-vulkan.so` with default visibility (they used to be `static`).        

This interacts badly with `ggml_backend_load_all()`:
1/ `ggml_backend_load_best("vulkan", ...)` scans the executable directory and dlopens `libggml-vulkan.so` found there.
2. In a non-GGML_BACKEND_DL build that library has no `ggml_backend_score` / `ggml_backend_init` symbols, so `load_backend()` returns and the handle is immediately **dlclosed**. This has always happened and used to be harmless.
3. If `libggml-vulkan.so` in the executable directory is a *regular file copy* rather than a symlink to the already-loaded `libggml-vulkan.so.0` (different inode — e.g. after installing with `cp`/`scp`, which dereference symlinks), glibc loads it as a **second copy** of the library.                         
4. The duplicate's dynamic relocations bind to the first copy's exported  globals (normal ELF interposition). At dlclose, the duplicate's static destructors therefore run against the **live** library's objects: `vk_instance_t::~vk_instance_t()` destroys the real `vk_instance`, leaving `device_indices` dangling.                                                                       
 
Any subsequent Vulkan device use then fails on an "impossible" assert; the exact site varies per run because the vector is dangling, e.g.:      

```
ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:14735: GGML_ASSERT(device < (int) vk_instance.device_indices.size()) failed                                                                         
ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:5173:  GGML_ASSERT(idx < vk_instance.device_indices.size()) failed                                                                                                
```

even though `ggml_vulkan: Found 1 Vulkan devices` was printed at startup.

### First Bad Commit

f172be756

title: Vulkan: ~78% decode throughput cliff at 131072 context — suballocation fragmentation; fixed via GGML_VK_SUBALLOCATION_BLOCK_SIZE=4 GiB
body:
# Vulkan: ~78% decode throughput cliff at 131072 context window — default ~1 GiB suballocation fragmentation; fixed via GGML_VK_SUBALLOCATION_BLOCK_SIZE=4 GiB

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24 GB, RDNA3, gfx1100) |
| OS / Driver | Windows 11, AMD proprietary driver |
| llama.cpp | 0.2.0-dev (build **10603**, commit c060ca974), Vulkan backend (ggml-vulkan.dll) |
| Model | Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid linear-attention, 64 layers), `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` (16.35 GiB) |
| Context | 131072 · KV cache `q8_0`/`q8_0` · `-fa on` · 4 slots unified pool |

## Summary

Decode throughput collapses from **~40 tok/s to ~8.9 tok/s** when the context window is raised from 98304 to 131072. The cliff is caused by the Vulkan backend's default **~1 GiB suballocation block size** fragmenting the large KV/compute pool into **30+ separate VkBuffers**. Setting `GGML_VK_SUBALLOCATION_BLOCK_SIZE=4294967296` restores full throughput at 131072.

## Reproduction

```powershell
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf `
  --ctx-size 131072 -fa on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --jinja `
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
```

Send a single-stream 1200-token completion (prompt ≈ 31 tokens), measure wall time.

## Results (same request, same binary, single GPU)

| ctx | KV dtype | suballoc block size | wall time | throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 65536 | f16 | default (1 GiB) | ~30 s | **40.4 tok/s** |
| 98304 | q8_0 | default | ~29 s | **40.8 tok/s** |
| **131072** | q8_0 | default | **~145 s** | **8.9 tok/s** ← cliff |
| **131072** | q8_0 | **4 GiB** | **~30 s** | **40.3 tok/s** ← restored |

Note: `llama-bench -p 512 -n 128` (small actual KV usage) stays at 40.4 tok/s even with q8 KV, so the cliff is tied to **pool allocation size**, not KV dtype.

## Diagnosis (`GGML_VK_MEMORY_LOGGER=1`)

At 131072, total device allocation is **21.55 GiB — fully in VRAM, no sysmem fallback** (total host = 152 MiB). The largest individual allocations are ≈ **1018 MiB each**, i.e. the pool is split into 30+ sub-blocks. At 98304 the same split stays below a critical block count and performance is unaffected.

No `OOM` / fallback warnings in logs. Memory location is not the issue — fragmentation of the pool into many independent `VkBuffer` objects is.

## Root-cause hypothesis

Decode at batch=1 touches the full KV/compute pool every step. With 30+ separate ~1 GiB sub-buffers, each step incurs per-buffer descriptor binding / submission overhead (and likely suboptimal memory access locality across disjoint buffers), multiplying the per-token cost by ~4.5×. Raising the suballocation block to 4 GiB keeps the pool in contiguous large buffers and eliminates the overhead.

## Workaround

```
GGML_VK_SUBALLOCATION_BLOCK_SIZE=4294967296
```

(before launching llama-server / llama-bench)

## Suggestions for maintainers

1. Consider raising the default suballocation block size, or sizing it relative to the KV pool (e.g. grow block size when the requested buffer exceeds N GiB).
2. Alternatively, allocate the KV cache as one contiguous buffer when it fits in VRAM, instead of splitting through the suballocator.
3. This appears to be a sibling of other "cliff at specific sizes" issues in the same backend: #25356 (fixed 8-token MMV dispatch thresholds) and #16759 (compute buffer jumps at specific context breakpoints).

---

**AI disclosure:** This report was researched and drafted with the assistance of an AI assistant (opencode). All measurements were performed locally on the machine described above; the evidence chain (memory logger output, A/B benchmark table) is reproducible with the commands provided.

title: Misc. bug: OpenVINO NPU: SIGSEGV/WeightlessCacheAttribute on Intel Core Ultra 7 255H (Linux)
body:
## Name and Version
```
$ ./build/bin/llama-cli --version
version: b10068-571d0d540
built with cc (GCC) 16.1.1 20250618 for x86_64-linux-gnu
```

OpenVINO 2026.2.1-2 (chaotic-aur), onetbb 2023.0.0-1
NPU driver 1.33.0, Intel AI Boost (arch 3720)
OS: Arch Linux, kernel 7.1.3

## Command line
```
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=NPU ./build/bin/llama-cli \
  -m Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -p "Hello" -n 10
```

## Problem description
Running llama.cpp with OpenVINO NPU backend on Intel Core Ultra 7 255H (Arrow Lake-P) results in two failure modes depending on NPUW configuration:

**Mode 1: Without NPUW** — SIGSEGV in `pthread_once` inside `libopenvino_intel_npu_plugin.so`. Appears to be a TBB race condition during NPU plugin initialization.

Backtrace:
```
#0  std::once_flag::_Prepare_execution (libllama-server-impl.so)
#1  pthread_once (libc.so.6)
#2  libopenvino_intel_npu_plugin.so
```

Minimal C++ test (`ov::Core` + `get_available_devices()`) works fine. Python bindings work fine. Crash only occurs during model compilation within llama.cpp context.

**Mode 2: With NPUW** (`NPU_USE_NPUW=YES`, `NPUW_WEIGHTS_BANK=shared`, etc.) — avoids SIGSEGV but fails with:
```
No "WeightlessCacheAttribute" has been found in any of the model's Constant nodes.
This attribute is required for running the "weights separation" flow.
```

The `ov::WeightlessCacheAttribute` class exists in `libopenvino.so` but its header is not installed in the distro package, so it cannot be added to weight `Constant` nodes from the OpenVINO backend.

Without `NPUW_WEIGHTS_BANK=shared`, falls back to Mode 1 (SIGSEGV).

## Related issues
Similar NPU-related issues exist, but our case is distinct:
- #25809 — first-run RoPE shape mismatch on Windows; second run succeeds via NPUW cache. Our crash is a SIGSEGV in driver init, not a shape error, and no second-run workaround.
- #25324 — same CPU (255H) on Windows, but crashes with `GGML_ASSERT` in CPU ops, not in NPU plugin.
- #23984 — f32/f16 type mismatch on NPU compilation, not a driver-level crash.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Build with `cmake -DGGML_OPENVINO=ON ..`
2. Download any small Llama GGUF (e.g., Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q4_K_M)
3. Run:
   ```
   GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=NPU ./build/bin/llama-simple -m model.gguf -p "Hello" -n 10
   ```
   Result: SIGSEGV
4. Run with NPUW config (current code sets `NPUW_WEIGHTS_BANK=shared`):
   Result: `WeightlessCacheAttribute` error

## Expected behavior
NPU inference works, similar to CPU-only build which produces 39 t/s on 1B model.

title: Feature Request: server: expose per-device memory usage (weights / context / compute)
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well. (master, c812c543f)
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

llama-server knows exactly how much memory it allocated on every device - model weights, context/KV cache, compute buffers, per GPU - plus each device's total and free memory. All of that only shows up as log lines. No API exposes it anywhere.

I want it reported per device, plus the model's layer count (the unit you split by). On `/metrics` (real output, M1 Pro):

```
llamacpp:memory_model_bytes{device="MTL0"} 83349984
llamacpp:memory_model_bytes{device="Host"} 13191648
llamacpp:memory_context_bytes{device="MTL0"} 0
llamacpp:memory_compute_bytes{device="MTL0"} 22559744
llamacpp:memory_total_bytes{device="MTL0"} 22906503168
llamacpp:memory_free_bytes{device="MTL0"} 22800187392
llamacpp:model_n_layer 12
```

And as JSON, since every other server endpoint speaks JSON:

```json
{
  "n_layer": 12,
  "data": [
    {"name": "MTL0", "model": 83349984, "context": 0, "compute": 22559744, "total": 22906503168, "free": 22800187392},
    {"name": "Host", "model": 13191648, "context": 0, "compute": 3684352}
  ]
}
```

`/metrics` serves Prometheus/Grafana; `GET /memory` serves programs. With a multimodal projector loaded, its per-device memory is reported too.

### Motivation

**My use case.** I run several llama-server instances sharing a set of GPUs. Before each launch I estimate how much memory it needs on each card, to pick a GPU and a context size. I have no way to check that estimate against what the server actually allocated - a bad estimate does not fail at launch, it fails later as a dead request.

**Today I parse the log.** A regex over the server log, environment variables to raise verbosity (the default level omits the report) and route the log to a file, and checked-in log fixtures to catch format drift between builds. It works. It is brittle and not a contract I want to rely on.

**Other people want this too.** In #23926 one user ships llama-server logs to Loki just to track per-GPU offloading and finds `-lv 4` far too noisy to store; another calls multi-GPU packing "guess work" while "completely blind".

**Nothing exposes it:**

| Surface | Per-device memory? | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `include/llama.h` | No. `llama_model_size()` is the whole model with no split. `llama_max_devices()` is a compile-time cap. | grep of all `LLAMA_API` |
| `llama_memory_*` in `llama.h` | No. That is the KV-cache sequence API (`seq_rm`, `seq_cp`, `pos_max`). | `llama.h:724-785` |
| `src/llama-ext.h` | Partly. `llama_get_memory_breakdown()` returns per buffer type, not per device. Header says staging, WIP, do not include elsewhere. | `llama-ext.h:1-5, 91` |
| HTTP | No. 50 registered method+path pairs, none carry memory. | `tools/server/server.cpp` route table |

Checked against a running server: `/props` is model and template metadata, `/metrics` is token counters, `/slots` has no memory field.

**The OS is not a substitute:**

- Apple Silicon: unified memory, so there is no per-process VRAM number to read at all. llama.cpp's own Metal backend reports `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize` as the device total (`ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-device.m:1043`) - 21845 MiB on this 32 GiB machine. A share of system RAM, not a pool you can attribute to a PID.
- Linux: the kernel's per-process counters (`drm-total-*`, `drm-resident-*`) are [optional per driver](https://docs.kernel.org/gpu/drm-usage-stats.html). Vendor tools fill the gap at one dependency and one output format per vendor.
- It is one number. No weights/context/compute split, so a wrong device split and an over-sized context look identical.
- `llama-bench` (#23208) and the router (#21231) need this in-process. They cannot shell out to `nvidia-smi`.

**The same aggregation is copy-pasted four times inside llama.cpp:**

| Location | What it is | Difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `common/fit.cpp:843-870` | inside `common_memory_breakdown_print` | counts only devices the model uses, buckets the rest into a separate row |
| `common/fit.cpp:77-97` | inside `common_get_device_memory_data_impl` | no separate bucket for unmatched buffer types |
| PR #23208 (`llama-bench`) | its own `std::map<ggml_backend_dev_t, size_t>` fold | sums into any device a buffer type resolves to, so it can disagree with the printed table for the same model |
| PR #21231 (router) | new `llama_context_device_memory()` plus its own `ggml_backend_dev_memory()` + margin logic | a third mechanism for the same question |

All of this is already computed, correctly - the server even prints it on exit (`tools/server/server.cpp:504`, only at trace verbosity). It is just logged. No API exposes it.

### Proposed Implementation https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26130

1. Move the aggregation out of the print function into a `common/` function that returns the rows. The print renders those rows, and `--fit`'s copy folds into it; `llama-bench` and the router can use it instead of theirs.
2. Report the rows on `/metrics` with a `device` label, and as JSON on `GET /memory` behind its own `--memory` flag (the `--slots` pattern: one flag per endpoint). Same internal task path.

Why `/metrics` for the Prometheus surface: it already exists, already gated, already works in router mode - and VRAM in Grafana is useful to more people than me. Why not `/props`: it is built to answer while the model is unloaded (`server-context.cpp:4526` makes touching the context a compile error), and free memory changes at runtime.

The `device` label is the backend's own name (`CUDA0`, `MTL0`, `Vulkan1`) - the same one `--list-devices` prints and `--device` accepts - so a caller can attribute memory to a specific card.

Flagging up front:

- `memory_total_bytes` / `memory_free_bytes` come straight from `ggml_backend_dev_memory()`, which has known bugs on some backends (#20858 Vulkan underflow, #24906 ROCm). Report as-is; fix those at the source.
- The `/metrics` writer formats every value as a `double`, which rounds past 6 significant digits. Byte counts need that fixed, and `prompt_tokens_total` is already affected past a million tokens.

I have both surfaces working, each behind its own flag - PR follows this issue.

title: ggml-backend-meta: `axis <= GGML_MAX_DIMS` off-by-one (inconsistent with ~21 other sites)
body:
`ggml/src/ggml-backend-meta.cpp:793` bounds-checks a dimension index with `<=`:

```c
if (ret.axis <= GGML_MAX_DIMS) { ... }   // accepts axis == GGML_MAX_DIMS
```

`ne[]` has `GGML_MAX_DIMS` elements, so `axis == GGML_MAX_DIMS` indexes one past the end. Roughly 21 other sites in the tree use `<` for the same comparison, so this one looks like a typo rather than intent.

**Not attacker-reachable as far as I can tell**, which is why I'm filing it as a plain bug rather than a security report: `ret.axis` comes from the host application's `get_split_state` callback, not from any GGUF file contents. So it requires an embedder to pass a bad axis, not a malicious model.

Suggested fix: change `<=` to `<` for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

Found while sweeping `GGML_MAX_*` uses for inconsistent comparison operators.

title: Feature Request: Improve SYCL Host-to-Device Memory Access
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

The SYCL backend currently does not use host-pinned memory, resulting in slow, costly copies from host to GPU.

|Computing Task|Total Time|Average|Time|Instance Count|SIMD Width|SVM Usage Type|Spill Memory Size|Host-to-Device|Device-to-Host|Global|Local|
|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
|zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopy|10.717s|0.490ms|21,881|||0|209.1 GB| 0.0 B|||
|zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopy|7.223s|0.330ms|21,898|||0|209.3 GB|0.0 B|||

The above is just a sample of the performance gain (VTune output). The first line is before the change, the second line is after.

1. Copy submit cost dropped 4.6s (12.1 → 7.45s). With pageable source, every zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopy call did synchronous page-pinning — 30-330 ms/call at 6-11 GB/s — and the host thread blocked on it. With pinned USM, submission is fire-and-forget; the host isn't stuck.
2. Pipeline de-stall. Total time drops more than the copy time alone because the host is the bottleneck: it stalls the pipeline while pinning, so compute cannot be fed on time. Remove the stall, the GPU stays fed continuously, and the whole graph completes earlier. 
3. Model load also benefits -- full-bandwidth load copies (28.7 vs 6-11 GB/s) shave the load phase too.

Result:

     | metric | master baseline | branch     | delta         |
     |--------|-----------------|------------|---------------|
     | pp2048 | 127.28 t/s      | 144.43 t/s | +13.5%        |
     | tg1    | 9.60 t/s        | 10.52 t/s  | decode normal |

This is running DS4F IQ2_XXS on an AMD 7950X w/128GB and an Intel B70.


### Motivation

Optimize the SYCL backend.

### Possible Implementation

[ggml-sycl-memory.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30850672/ggml-sycl-memory.txt)

@arthw This is a diff containing the proposed code changes. The `get_max_size` implementation is required in order to properly allocate large blocks of host memory for larger models such as DS4F. Without it, the code silently falls back to allocating unpinned memory.

title: Eval bug: DSV4 state_read() clears the compressed KV cache of all sequences, silently desyncing other slots
body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 10276 (6ea215d17)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

The defect is still present in current `master` (`cd0fa60`, b10286) — see line references below.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

6x RTX 5090 (sm120), x86_64

### Models

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (unsloth `UD-Q3_K_XL`), with the DSpark drafter (`--spec-type draft-dspark`).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama_kv_cache_dsv4::state_read()` clears the **entire** CSA/HCA/LID compressed caches — i.e. all sequences — before reading back the state of a **single** sequence:

```cpp
// src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1594-1604 (master cd0fa60)
    kv_raw->state_read(io, seq_id, flags);          // <-- correctly scoped to seq_id

    if (!partial_only) {
        kv_csa->clear(true);                        // <-- cache-wide: ALL sequences
        kv_hca->clear(true);
        kv_lid->clear(true);

        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_csa.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_hca.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_lid.get(), seq_id, flags);
    }
```

`llama_kv_cache::clear(bool)` is cache-wide, while the restore of the raw cache immediately above it is scoped to `seq_id`. The class already provides a sequence-scoped helper for exactly this:

```cpp
// src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1671
void llama_kv_cache_dsv4::clear_compressed(llama_seq_id seq_id, bool data);
```

That helper was introduced by #25521 ("DeepseekV4: clear cache only for seq rather than full", `13f2b28b0`) specifically so that per-sequence operations stop wiping the whole compressed cache, and `seq_rm()` (line 1447) and `seq_keep()` (line 1481) both use it correctly. `state_read()` is the one path that still does a full clear.

**Consequence.** With `--parallel N` (N > 1, which is also the server's auto default of 4), restoring the state of one sequence destroys the compressed KV of every *other* sequence while leaving their raw KV intact. Those sequences are left silently desynced — no error and no crash, they simply continue decoding against zeroed compressed caches. The user-visible symptom is one slot abruptly losing its context while other slots are being restored.

Affected paths are any single-sequence `state_read`: `POST /slots/{id}?action=restore`, `--prompt-cache`/checkpoint reload, and `llama_state_seq_set_data()` in the public API.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `llama-server` with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--parallel 2` (or the auto default of 4) and `--slot-save-path <dir>`.
2. Build up a conversation on slot 0 and a second, different conversation on slot 1.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
4. Continue the conversation on **slot 1** — its continuation no longer reflects its own history.

**Suggested fix** — use the existing seq-scoped helper, which already treats `seq_id < 0` as "all":

```cpp
    if (!partial_only) {
        clear_compressed(seq_id, true);

        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_csa.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_hca.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_lid.get(), seq_id, flags);
    }
```

**Disclosure about how this was found.** This is from code inspection while investigating unrelated context-corruption on our rig, not from a captured reproduction — we run `--cache-ram 0` and avoid the restore path, so I do not have a log of the failure itself. The control flow above is unambiguous, but I have not bisected a live repro, hence no log section below. Happy to run the reproduction above and report back if that would help.

**Note on similar-looking reports.** #25171 ("forgets everything") and #25259 ("forgot context when hit cache or use checkpoint in long context") describe the same user-visible symptom, but both were opened (2026-06-30 and 2026-07-03) *before* the commit below landed, so this is not their original cause. Mentioning them only because the symptom class is identical and multi-slot users hitting it today may now be running into this instead.

### First Bad Commit

`91d2fc387` — "llama_dsv4: write only used rows in state" (#25325, 2026-07-20). That commit added the three cache-wide clears inside `state_read`; the patch hunk is `@@ -1366,6 +1419,10 @@ void llama_kv_cache_dsv4::state_read`. Before it, `state_read()` did not clear the compressed caches at all.

### Relevant log output

```
Not applicable — reported from code inspection, see disclosure above.
```

title: Eval bug: temp-0 tool-calling is nondeterministic for hybrid Qwen3.6-A3B on Vulkan — flips with prompt-cache mode and across restarts
body:
### Name and Version

llama-server, build 221f0f6 (2026-08-02), Vulkan backend
GPU: Intel Arc Pro B60 24GB (Battlemage), Mesa 26.1.6 (VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2 available), kernel 7.0.0-28-generic

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server --model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --alias qwen36-coder \
  --device Vulkan0 --port 8091 --host 0.0.0.0 --jinja -fa on \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --ctx-size 131072 --parallel 2 \
  --kv-unified --n-gpu-layers 999 --threads 8 --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 1024
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**With a hybrid-recurrent model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gated-DeltaNet), reusing cached prompt state can silently drop tool-calling**: at `temperature: 0`, the *identical* OpenAI-compat request emits a well-formed `tool_calls` array when processed with `"cache_prompt": false`, and returns plain prose (no tool call, no error) when cached state is reused. Nothing is logged; the response is otherwise normal — on an agentic lane this silently degrades from "controls things" to "talks about things".

Repro shape (three requests, `temperature 0`, two simple function tools defined; full script available):

1. Fresh server start. Requests with default caching → a request like *"What's the weather in Tokyo right now?"* (expect `get_weather`) returns **no tool_calls** on some post-restart cache states, while *"Turn on the kitchen light"* (expect `control_light`) may or may not fire.
2. Same requests with `"cache_prompt": false` → **always correct** `tool_calls` (dozens of runs, never a failure).
3. After a `cache_prompt:false` pass, default-cache requests *sometimes* recover (the clean full prefill appears to repair the reusable state) — and sometimes don't. Observed both outcomes across several restarts on the same build/flags.

Observed on q8_0 **and** q4_0 KV cache (`-fa on` in both cases), so not KV-quant-specific. The failure correlates with which cached state a request lands on, not with the request content.

This looks related to the hybrid/recurrent checkpointing work (#22384 fixed checkpoint *restore* for DeltaNet/Mamba — this build includes that fix and restore does function; prompt-cache hit rates are otherwise good). Possibly the reused recurrent state is subtly wrong in a way that only shows up as degraded structured-output behavior rather than incoherence. Notably, the same user-visible symptom (prefix-cache hit ⇒ loss of tool calling on Qwen3.6 hybrid) has been reported independently against a different engine (omlx issue #825), which suggests the hybrid-arch state-reuse pattern itself is delicate here.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown — first observed on 221f0f6 in production use; we have no earlier-build A/B for this symptom.

### Relevant log output

```
# temperature 0, tools defined, same server process, minutes apart:

# default cache_prompt:
FAIL weather: NO tool call emitted            # message.content is plain prose
PASS light: control_light({"entity":"kitchen light","state":"on"})

# cache_prompt: false (same requests):
PASS light: control_light({"entity":"kitchen light","state":"on"})
PASS weather: get_weather({"location":"Tokyo"})

# a later restart, after one full clean (cache_prompt:false) pass, back on default cache:
FAIL weather: NO tool call emitted            # "healing" did not persist this time
```

Happy to run instrumented builds, capture `--verbose` slot logs, or bisect prompts further — the setup is a persistent homelab server and the repro harness is scripted.

title: speculative: draft-dflash draft acceptance collapses under concurrent sequences (-np 16 pathological, -np 4 healthy, --spec-draft-n-max 1 recovers)
body:
### Summary

`--spec-type draft-dflash` works well at low concurrency, but under concurrent slots the **draft model's predictions get corrupted**, draft acceptance collapses, and throughput goes into reverse (slower than no speculation). We traced this on an AMD gfx1151 APU across two ROCm versions and pinned down that the corruption **scales with the number of concurrently-drafting sequences, not with batch token count, server slot count, or draft length alone**:

| server `-np` | active requests | `--spec-draft-n-max` | noise-block batch | per-slot draft acceptance | aggregate throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 4 | 15 | 64 tok | **0.51 – 0.66** (healthy) | healthy |
| **16** | **4** | 15 | 64 tok | **0.51 – 0.66** (bit-identical to the row above, same seed) | healthy |
| 8 | 8 | 15 | 128 tok | 0.11 – 0.46 (degraded) | degraded |
| 16 | 16 | 7 | 128 tok | 0.22 – 0.74 (bimodal) | bad |
| 16 | 16 | 15 | 256 tok | **0.06 – 0.49** (bimodal; sustained load collapses to **0.0018**) | ~17–21 tok/s vs **37 tok/s** no-spec baseline |
| 16 | 16 | **1** | 32 tok | **0.83 – 0.92** | **~80 tok/s (2.2× the no-spec baseline)** |

Key observations that localize the defect:

1. **Per-slot corruption is established during prefill and persists for the request's lifetime.** 16 *identical* requests (same prompt, seed, temperature) produce an ~8× spread in acceptance across slots, visible from the very first speculative tick. The draft model's top-1 confidence is bimodal per slot: median 0.25 on "broken" slots vs 0.92–0.98 on "healthy" ones.
2. **It is not the server's slot configuration** — a `-np 16` server with only 4 in-flight requests produces bit-identical results to a `-np 4` server.
3. **It is not the drafter's intrinsic quality** — with `--spec-draft-n-max 1` the same 16-way load accepts 83–92 % of drafts and beats the no-spec baseline by 2.2×.
4. **It is not a ROCm-version regression** — identical pathology on ROCm 7.2.1 and 7.14.0 (we cannot test CUDA here; see "ask" at the end).

### Git commit

- Verified at `0b1bad14ff204627636aeb1de22ddcd5acb859d4` (2026-08-11).
- **Still reproduces on current master `0177dcc7300bad8914bb838baabce87899812491` (2026-08-15, freshly built)**: 16 identical concurrent requests → the same bimodal per-slot acceptance (0.05–0.50, broken slots waste 500–977 drafts per 160-token request); the 4-concurrent control on the same server recovers (0.19–0.61). The numbers below are from the pinned build.

Build: `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DROCM_PATH=…` (Release, GCC 13.3, `GGML_HIP_GRAPHS=ON` default).

Hardware/runtime: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S iGPU (gfx1151, 96 GB unified), kernel 6.17, ROCm 7.14.0 (side-by-side 7.2.1 with identical results).

Models: Muse-Glimmer-30B target (Q4_K "kquant" GGUF, ~17 GB, all layers on GPU) + the matching DFlash draft GGUF (`general.architecture = dflash`, 5 layers, `block_size=16`, 5 extracted target layers). Any supported dense target + DFlash pair should reproduce the concurrency dependence.

### Command line

```bash
llama-server -m muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-17gb.gguf -ngl 999 \
  -np 16 -c 131072 --jinja \
  -md dflash-kquant.gguf -ngld 99 \
  --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 15 \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --seed 42 \
  --port 8080 > server.log 2>&1
```

Reproduce (the server log is the instrument — `/metrics` spec counters stay 0 on these builds):

```bash
# 16 identical concurrent streaming requests
seq 16 | xargs -P16 -I{} curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain in detail why the sky is blue."}],
       "max_tokens":160,"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":64,"seed":42}' >/dev/null

grep 'draft acceptance' server.log
```

Controls (each on a fresh server):

- `-P4` instead of `-P16` (same `-np 16` server) → acceptance recovers to ~0.5–0.66.
- `--spec-draft-n-max 1` with `-P16` → acceptance 0.83–0.92, ~2.2× no-spec throughput.
- `-np 4` server, `-P4` → bit-identical to the `-np 16`/`-P4` run (same seed).

### Problem description & logs

Expected: draft acceptance roughly constant w.r.t. concurrency (speculative decoding is lossless; batching drafts from many sequences should not change per-sequence predictions), and DFlash at `-np 16` to at least not be slower than no speculation.

Actual (16 identical concurrent requests, fresh server, `0b1bad1`):

```
slot print_timing: id  1 | draft acceptance = 0.05333 (    4 accepted /    75 generated), mean len =  1.80
slot print_timing: id  7 | draft acceptance = 0.25424 (   45 accepted /   177 generated), mean len =  3.50
slot print_timing: id 10 | draft acceptance = 0.49074 (   53 accepted /   108 generated), mean len =  6.89
slot print_timing: id 12 | draft acceptance = 0.19048 (   44 accepted /   231 generated), mean len =  3.44
slot print_timing: id  0 | draft acceptance = 0.07289 (   32 accepted /   439 generated), mean len =  2.03
...
spec statistics: draft-dflash: #calls(b,g,a) = 16 31 294, #gen tokens = 3758, #acc tokens = 509,
                #mean acc len = 2.73, dur(b,g,a) = 0.020, 4133.404, 0.072 ms
```

Under sustained long-generation load this collapses completely — a 16×512, 5-rep run on ROCm 7.2.1 was aborted after 5 h 16 min with **3,270,000 drafted / 6,060 accepted (0.18 %)**.

Secondary symptoms at `-np 16` (measured on the same runs):

- Prompt processing with DFlash injection runs at ~57 ms/token (~17.5 tok/s) vs ~23 ms/token (~43 tok/s) without DFlash at the same `-np` — the per-sequence sequential `llama_encode` + inject `llama_decode` in `process()` is paid once per sequence per batch.
- Steady-state speculative tick is 1.15–1.5 s; `draft()` alone averages 133 ms per call (256-token noise block); per-token time grows ~3× over a 320-token request (207 → 570 ms/token), i.e. it decays as generations lengthen.
- The HIP backend logs `CUDA graph warmup reset` 1–2× per tick (54–194 per run) as batch composition changes, adding graph re-capture churn.

### Analysis (pointers, not conclusions)

- The corruption tracks **how many sequences share the batched non-causal noise-block decode** (`common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash::draft()`, one `llama_decode` with `n_seq × (n_max+1)` tokens): 4 seqs → clean, 8 → degraded, 16 → collapsed; same total token count with 16 seqs (`n_max=7`) is still corrupted, which is why we suspect per-sequence state (KV injection / attention mask / sampler alignment) rather than raw batch size.
- `common_speculative_process()` is invoked after **every** target decode ([tools/server/server-context.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/0b1bad14ff204627636aeb1de22ddcd5acb859d4/tools/server/server-context.cpp) `decode()`), including verification batches, and processes sequences sequentially — under a mixed 16-slot prefill this interleaves 16 encode+inject rounds with concurrent drafting.
- Ruled out: slot reuse / prompt-cache state (fresh server, cold slots); the "Drafts may degrade" prefill-ubatch path (no such warnings); drafter quality (n_max=1 accepts 0.87+); ROCm version (7.2.1 ≡ 7.14.0).
- **Ask:** could someone reproduce on CUDA? If it reproduces there, the defect is in the core spec-decode/masking path; if not, it points at the HIP path (and we can help bisect kernels).

### Workaround

At high concurrency either cap active requests (≤4) or use `--spec-draft-n-max 1` — measured **~80 tok/s aggregate vs 37 tok/s** no-spec baseline at `-np 16` (acceptance 0.83–0.92). Documenting this knob next to DFlash multi-slot guidance would already help users.

Unrelated observation while testing: at `temperature 1.0` the server sometimes terminates completed streams with HTTP 500 `"The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format"` — happy to file that separately with logs.

### Related

- #25117 (DFlash ~2× slower than baseline on the same APU class, `-np 1`, MoE target)
- #26741 / #26756 (multi-slot + speculative decoding corrupting KV state — same symptom class)
- DFlash tracking discussion: #21569

title: spec + vulkan: Performance Drop with MTP n-max > 1 and -np > 1
body:
### Name and Version from master: 2c6b141efb3b0868fd39d3cae73f69606e1d654c Build / running in docker, arch-base image, host has kernel 7.1.8, RADV/MESA 26.1.7. ### Operating systems Linux ### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected? llama-server ### Command line ```shell llama-server in docker with compose: llama-server-vulkan-arch: build: context: . target: server dockerfile: .devops/vulkan-arch.Dockerfile container_name: llamacpp ipc: host networks: - ai_stack ports: - "11435:8080" environment: - GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2,1 - GGML_VK_ALLOW_GRAPHICS_QUEUE=1 volumes: - /mnt/workdrive/llamacpp/models:/models - /mnt/workdrive/llamacpp/models_rpc.ini:/app/models.ini - /mnt/workdrive/llamacpp/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface group_add: - video devices: - "/dev/kfd:/dev/kfd" - "/dev/dri:/dev/dri" entrypoint: ["./llama-server"] command: > --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --models-dir /models --models-preset /app/models.ini --models-max 2 --sleep-idle-seconds 6000 --metrics --load-mode none --offline --log-verbosity 3 --sse-ping-interval 15 restart: unless-stopped Model ini: qwen3-8-27b] cache-ram = 14336 ctx-checkpoints = 4 checkpoint-min-step = 8192 main-gpu = 0 parallel = 3 batch-size = 4096 ubatch-size = 512 kv-unified = false spec-type = draft-mtp spec-draft-n-max = 1 spec-draft-n-min = 0 hf = unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL ctx-size = 491520 temp = 1.0 top-p = 0.95 top-k = 20 min-p = 0.0 presence-penalty = 0.0 repeat-penalty = 1.0 cache-type-k = q8_0 cache-type-v = q8_0 flash-attn = true split-mode = layer tensor-split = 50,50,0 jinja = true reasoning-preserve = true reasoning-effort = medium reasoning-budget = 20000 image-min-tokens = 1024 no-mmproj-offload = true ``` ### Problem description & steps to reproduce On vulkan with np>1 and actually dispatching parallel sessions, along with model-native MTP (tested with Q3.6-27B and Q3.8-27B, different quants, from UD-Q4-XL to Q6_K) the performance collapses when n-max for the draft is set to > 1. My setup has 2xR9700, and ROCM seems to scale better, especially for np > 2, but I only tested until np = 4. See below. Single session works fine as expected, and also scales well with n-max, depending on the workload of course. With very large n-max (5-6) i sometime even see a spike to 60TPS+ when the predictions hit the spot. But mostly its in the 42-46TPS range single session. Setup / Contig notes included, mind that I rund with large context, 3x160k(*1024). This has also been reported in other issues, but I want to collect this here, so we can maybe focus efforts, debugging, etc. to arrive at a root cause. @0cc4m this follows up my statements in the dflash2 PR; hope this is a better home and naming you here since you mentioned that you are not aware of an issue with the scaling currently. Nvidia does not seem to be affected, but AMD seems to be, and one report in the dflash2 PR #27342 from one intel user did show the same behavior. I noticed that MTP/Dflash2 had the same issue, so my speculation is somewhere else, either in the vulkan backend or in some interworking between the sessions, spec and the backend. I tried to seach around, and here are some issues which might be related and/or have content / benchmarks which show the issue. #26360 (Feature Request Vulkan) #23774 (MTP Perf Deg Vulkan) #24066 (General Vulkan Perf drop) #26663 (Vulkan Ops Profiles RDNA4) #27181 (Helpful links to other Projects, also RDNA4 specific) #21043 (Lots of performance measurements, also some with the symptom, but also without, RDNA4) I'm happy to assist with any kind of debug output needed, and test patches. title: Feature Request: --reasoning-budget like argument to control the budget based on the conversation length
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

A `--reasoning-budget` like argument that allows us to control the budget based on the conversation length. There could also be another argument that does the same, but based only on the current prompt.

Examples:

`--reasoning-budget 0.5`: the max reasoning tokens will be 50% of the conversation lenght;
`--reasoning-budget 0.5+4000`: the max reasoning tokens will be 50% of the conversation length plus 4000 tokens;
`--reasoning-budget 0.5-2300`: the max reasoning tokens will be 50% of the conversation length minus 2300 tokens;
`--reasoning-budget-current 0.3`: the max reasoning tokens will be 30% of the current prompt lenght;
`--reasoning-budget-current 0.3+4000`: the max reasoning tokens will be 30% of the current prompt length plus 4000 tokens;
`--reasoning-budget-current 0.3-2300`: the max reasoning tokens will be 30% of the current prompt length minus 2300 tokens

### Motivation

Having a fixed reasoning budget might not be good for all tasks. Imagine that you send a 50k prompt. Having a reasoning budget of only 4k could probably be not enough. If the reasoning budget is too low, it will be the same as not having reasoning at all in practice. If the reasoning budget is too high, it kinda defeats the purpose of having a reasoning budget.

```shell
podman run --rm -it ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server -hf ggml-org/gemma-3-4b-it-GGUF
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

After running the command with the `-hf` argument,  `llama-server` will start downloading the model from hugging face. Before the download is complete, the container cannot be interrupted with ctrl+c/SIGINT. Once the download finishes and the server starts, ctrl+c cleanly terminates the server with the message from the signal handler "cleaning up before exit...".

Looking at the source code, it seems that the issue was caused by the [signal handler](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/70adb1b4cea5ee39f867792c78dc59320921eda7/tools/server/server.cpp#L486) being installed too late. 

It's not hard to work around this issue by passing the `--init` flag to podman or bake `tini` as the entrypoint for the dockerfile, although it would be nicer to have the signal handler properly installed.
