title: Feature Request: Vulkan: retune coopmat/MMQ tiles for RDNA3.5 / Strix Halo prefill
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Add a Strix Halo (gfx1151 / RDNA3.5) specific tuning for the Vulkan KHR_cooperative_matrix (coopmat) matrix-multiply tiles, to make prompt processing (prefill) faster on models like Qwen3.8-27B.

Today the AMD coopmat path uses one generic large tile for all AMD cards; Strix Halo is an integrated GPU with its own cache sizes and wavefront behavior, so it should get its own tile sizes, picked by measuring.

## Measurements / observations

Setup: Radeon 8050S (32 CU), RADV / Mesa 26.1.8, `uma:1`, Qwen3.8-27B
`UD-Q4_K_S`, `-p 128 -n 32 -b 128 -ub 128 -r 3 -fa on -ngl 99`:

- `pp128: 194.13 ± 1.45 t/s`, `tg32: 12.86 ± 0.10 t/s`
- Prefill is >90% GEMM (`MUL_MAT`), all on the coopmat/MMQ path:

| shape | iq4_xs | q4_K | q5_K |
|---|---|---|---|
| m=17408, k=5120 (FFN up/gate) | 69x 2087us (10.9 TFLOPS) | 17x 2084us (11.0 TFLOPS) | 14x 2045us (11.2 TFLOPS) |
| m=5120, k=17408 (FFN down) | 29x 2587us (8.8 TFLOPS) | 12x 2533us (9.0 TFLOPS) | 14x 2718us (8.4 TFLOPS) |

Path checks (same flags, prove which code runs):

- `GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT=1` → pp128 falls to 106.21 (-45%), tg32
  unchanged. So prefill runs on coopmat, decode does not.
- `GGML_VK_DISABLE_INTEGER_DOT_PRODUCT=1` → pp128 falls to 174.53
  (-10%), tg32 unchanged. So the integer-dot MMQ path is active in
  prefill with a modest share.

History: PR #18749 (generic AMD large tile `{256,128,128}`) gave
+35-75% prefill on 8060S. That tile reuses medium TM/TN/TK values and
was never specialized for gfx1151. The card reports only `16x16x16`
fp16/int8 coopmat shapes (verified with a Vulkan probe), so there is
room left in workgroup geometry, subgroup size, and LDS traffic.

## Related files and functions

All in `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/` (line numbers at HEAD `002a12ad2`):

- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:4540-4545` — AMD+coopmat large-tile override
  (this is where a gfx1151 branch goes)
- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:4490-4498` — `tm/tn/tk` from probed `coopmat_m/n/k`
- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:4568-4627` — shared-memory guards that silently
  disable tiles that do not fit (must check when adding tiles)
- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:4166-4289` — `ggml_vk_matmul_shmem_support` /
  `ggml_vk_matmul_int_shmem_support` (LDS budget math)
- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:7320-7327` — AMD tile enables (`mul_mat_id_l`
  stays `false`, see #23106)
- `vulkan-shaders/mul_mm.comp:43-47,161-192,383-386` — `LOAD_VEC_A`,
  spec constants, hardcoded A-RowMajor / B-ColumnMajor coop loads
- `vulkan-shaders/mul_mmq.comp:103-104` — `LOAD_VEC_A/B` for int path
- `vulkan-shaders/mul_mmq_funcs.glsl` — int-dot dequant + dot
- Unmerged prototype branch: `0cc4m/vulkan-coopmat-int8`
  (`mul_mmq_cm1.comp`, int8 coopmat MMQ, tip `918f32dcf`)

## Proposed behavior

1. Detect gfx1151 narrowly (AMD + coopmat + not proprietary driver +
   `uma` + 64 KiB shared memory + `STRIX_HALO` device name) and give it
   its own `l/m_warptile_mmq*` values, found by measurement: first
   BM/BN/BK geometry (including non-square), then subgroup 32 vs 64,
   then `LOAD_VEC_A` / LDS bank padding per quant type.
2. Generic AMD path and all other vendors/drivers stay exactly as now.
3. Longer term: rebase and evaluate the int8-coopmat prototype branch,
   starting with NVFP4 (simple dequant, already in the upstream MMQ
   type lists) before attempting `iq4_xs`.

## Notes
- Assisted by a coding AI agent
- Current Commit: 002a12ad25503a93501b2e188c360029830a241a

### Motivation

Prefill at `n=128` is compute-bound (about 380 FLOP/byte vs a machine balance of about 325), while decode (`n=1`) is memory-bandwidth-bound near the ~200 GB/s wall. So tile tuning moves prefill/TTFT without being able to hurt decode much and the per-shape table above shows prefill GEMM at ~9-11 TFLOPS against a ~65 TFLOPS WMMA roof, i.e. mostly headroom. Prior art (#18749) already proved tiles alone can move Strix Halo prefill by tens of percent.

### Possible Implementation

- Step 1: sweep `l_mmq` BM/BN/BK (`{256,128,128}` vs `{256,64,128}`
  vs `{128,128,128}` vs `{256,128,64}`) and `m_mmq` at `n=128`;
  keep `s` tiles stable; verify each candidate survives the
  `matmul_shmem_support` guard via `GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER=1`.
- Step 2: clone the winner with `WARP 64 -> 32` (RDNA3 is natively
  wave32; current tiles use 64).
- Step 3: `LOAD_VEC_A` 4 -> 8 for `q4_K`/`q5_K`/`iq4_xs` int paths,
  `SHMEM_STRIDE_PAD` 8 vs 4/16 on the winning tile.
- Step 4: measure (do not assume) B-operand layout per dtype; expect
  ~0% on fp16.
- Step 5: rebase `0cc4m/vulkan-coopmat-int8`, `test-backend-ops` all
  covered quants, measure pp128/512/2048 + tg32; NVFP4 first, then
  consider `iq4_xs` (43.8% of prefill, covered nowhere today).
- Bench rule: matched `-b/-ub` flags, cool-downs, tg32 guard on every
  step, `test-backend-ops` on every tile change. Tiles must stay
  bit-identical (same accumulation order) or pass greedy exact-match
  (`--temp 0 --top-k 1 --seed 42`).

title: Feature Request: Add /think command to control reasoning and hide <think> tags
body: ### Prerequisites - [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well. - [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md). - [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed). - [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share. ### Feature Description When using reasoning-capable models such as Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B, the console currently displays empty or populated reasoning tags: This adds unnecessary noise to the CLI, especially when thinking is disabled or the model produces no visible reasoning. There is also no convenient way to change the thinking/reasoning level directly during an interactive session. ### Motivation Add a /think command to control reasoning dynamically. For example: /think off /think minimal /think low /think medium /think high /think max /think ultra Running /think without an argument could display the current state: > /think Thinking: off When thinking is disabled, ... should not be displayed in the console at all. When thinking is enabled, the CLI could either hide the reasoning content by default or provide an optional way to display it, for example: /think show /think hide Ideally, the selected thinking level should be applied without having to restart or reload the model. This would make reasoning-capable models much cleaner and easier to use interactively, particularly fast local models where users often want to switch between direct responses and deeper reasoning. ### Possible Implementation

title: bug: Qwen3.8 DFlash/MTP speculative emits OOB token id == n_vocab (248320) on Vulkan
body:
## Summary
On AMD Strix Point (`gfx1150`) Vulkan with llama.cpp **b10724**, Qwen3.8-27B + z-lab DFlash2 (or ggml MTP draft) fails decode with:

```
init: invalid token[1] = 248320
decode: failed to initialize batch
```

**248320 equals `tokenizer.ggml.tokens` array length** — valid token ids are `0..248319`. This looks like a classic off-by-one in draft sampling / logits indexing.

## Environment
- GPU: AMD Strix Point `gfx1150`, Vulkan/RADV
- Runtime: llama.cpp **b10724** (also reproduced earlier on b10666)
- Target: `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` (architecture `qwen35`)
- Draft A: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-GGUF` → `Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M.gguf` (`dflash`)
- Draft B: Unsloth `mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf` (`qwen35`) — same `248320` with ggml MTP
- Flags: `--spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 2` (or `draft-mtp`)

Note: Muse-Glimmer + DFlash on the same binary/hardware **works** (different vocab/arch ~200k). Vanilla Qwen3.8 without speculation is fine (~4.3 t/s).

## GGUF metadata (streaming count of `tokenizer.ggml.tokens`)
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| n_vocab (`tokenizer.ggml.tokens` len) | **248320** |
| bos_token_id | 248044 |
| eos_token_id | 248046 |

Same n_vocab / bos / eos on target, DFlash draft, and MTP draft.

## Expected
Draft sampling never emits token id `>= n_vocab`.

## Actual
First decode step emits token **248320** (exactly `n_vocab`). Server returns HTTP 500 / "Invalid input batch."

## Suggested fix
1. Clamp draft token ids to `[0, n_vocab - 1]` after sampling in the DFlash/MTP verify path.
2. Audit `qwen35` / `dflash` draft-head logits indexing for `< n_vocab` vs `<= last index` (or `argmax` over `n_vocab+1` slots).

## Repro
```bash
llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --device Vulkan0 -ngl 999 --ctx-size 8192 \
  --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --flash-attn on \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --no-webui
# POST /v1/chat/completions → 500; log shows invalid token 248320
```

## Related
- #27812 fixed Vulkan graph-optimizer wrong tokens for speculative acceptance (merged); this is a separate hard OOB failure that remains on tip after that fix.
- Unsloth Qwen3.8 MTP on the same stack loads without `248320` in one layout but reports **accept rate 0.0** (possible related draft-head issue; see also #28097).

Happy to provide full server logs / GGUF SHA if useful.

title: Misc. bug: CPU f32 GELU uses GGML_GELU_FP16, loses precision
body:
### Name and Version

ggml v0.24.0, commit 456172e.

### Abstract

I was porting laya-vision to ggml, and found the network lose precision compared to the PyTorch version. (the project: https://git.sr.ht/~iacore/ggml-question)

It turns out that f32 GELU on CPU converts input to FP16 first, which loses precision over actual f32 GLEU.

### Reproduction repo

Here is a standalone program linked directly against ggml, CPU backend, no model or server
involved.

https://github.com/iacore/ggml-gelu-f16-repro

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Command line

```sh
cc -O2 -I <ggml>/include repro.c -o repro \
   -L <ggml-build>/ggml/src -lggml -lggml-base -lggml-cpu -lm
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<ggml-build>/ggml/src ./repro
```

The program builds one `GGML_OP_GELU` and one `GGML_OP_GELU_ERF` over the same f32 input tensor,
runs the graph on the CPU backend, and compares both against the exact float32 formula.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`src/ggml-cpu/vec.h:46` defines `GGML_GELU_FP16` unconditionally, and under it the **f32** GELU
does not evaluate its formula. It rounds the input to half precision, indexes a table, and converts
the result back:

```c
#ifdef GGML_GELU_FP16
inline static void ggml_vec_gelu_f32(const int n, float * y, const float * x) {
    uint16_t t;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        if (x[i] <= -10.0f) {
            y[i] = 0.0f;
        } else if (x[i] >= 10.0f) {
            y[i] = x[i];
        } else {
            ggml_fp16_t fp16 = GGML_CPU_FP32_TO_FP16(x[i]);
            memcpy(&t, &fp16, sizeof(uint16_t));
            y[i] = GGML_CPU_FP16_TO_FP32(ggml_table_gelu_f16[t]);
        }
    }
}
```

The table is filled at `src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:3883` with
`GGML_CPU_FP32_TO_FP16(ggml_gelu_f32(f))`. So one element takes x -> f16 -> gelu -> f16 -> f32:
rounded to half precision twice, once on the way in and once on the way out.

`GGML_GELU_QUICK_FP16`, defined on the line below, means `ggml_gelu_quick` gets the same treatment.
`GGML_OP_GELU_ERF` is not affected: `ggml_vec_gelu_erf_f32` has no table path.

Measured against the exact float32 form of the same formula, 4096 values over the stated range:

| input range | max abs | max rel | elements over 1.2e-4 rel |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [-12, 12] | 3.9024e-3 | 3.6916e-3 | 1611 / 4096 |
| [-10, 10] | 3.90e-3 | 2.70e-3 | 1917 / 4096 |
| [-5, 5] | 1.95e-3 | 3.65e-3 | 2548 / 4096 |
| [-1, 1] | 3.20e-4 | 7.52e-4 | 2833 / 4096 |

Control on the same inputs: `GGML_OP_GELU_ERF` against the erf formula gives **0.0000e+00** rms
relative error, bit-exact.

The error is broad rather than localized -- roughly 4e-4 relative on nearly every element, which is
f16 epsilon (2^-11 = 4.9e-4). It is not one or two bad elements.

I have not traced which models in this repository route through `GGML_OP_GELU` in f32 on CPU, or by
how much their output changes. The error is on the order of the activation's own precision, so it
may well be an acceptable trade for avoiding a `tanhf` per element. I am reporting the behavior and
the test's blind spot, not claiming model output is visibly wrong.

### Why test-backend-ops does not catch it

`tests/test-backend-ops.cpp:3940` sets the GELU tolerance and states an assumption the code does not
satisfy:

```c
// gelu shader uses exp form, CPU uses tanhf
default:            return op == GGML_UNARY_OP_GELU ? 5e-7 : 1e-7;
```

"CPU uses tanhf" is not true under `GGML_GELU_FP16`.

Separately, `test_unary_mul` compares with `err()`, which is `nmse(...)`
(`test-backend-ops.cpp:298`, `:1191`) -- a signal-to-noise ratio, not a max error. The measured NMSE
is 2.9e-8, seventeen times under the 5e-7 tolerance, so the test passes.

That is the wrong metric for this shape of error rather than a tolerance that is merely loose. NMSE
catches one large absolute error loudly; a broad, small *relative* error contributes about
(relative error)^2 and disappears. This is the second shape.

A max-relative-error check, or an NMSE bound chosen for f32 rather than f16, would have caught it.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. `GGML_GELU_FP16` has been unconditional for a long time and this is not a recent
regression.

### Relevant log output

```
ggml backend: CPU   revision: v0.24.0 (commit 456172e)
ggml_gelu      max|abs|=3.9024e-03  max|rel|=3.6916e-03  over 1.2e-4 rel: 1611/4096
ggml_gelu_erf  rms relative error vs the erf formula: 0.0000e+00   (the control)
nmse (what test-backend-ops compares, tolerance 5e-7): 2.8987e-08
```

title: Qwen3-VL: mtmd vision embeddings carry ~5× HF precision-floor noise → reproducible accuracy drop vs transformers (quant/backend/version-independent)
body:
# [DRAFT] Upstream issue for ggml-org/llama.cpp — Qwen3-VL vision-path numeric noise


## Environment
- Models: Qwen3-VL-8B dense fine-tune (LoRA merged, bf16), converted with current `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` (mmproj: f16, also tested f32).
- Runtimes tested: b10707 (Vulkan, 0.7 box), b10909 (CUDA, 52 box), and a build of PR #21103 head on its merge-base (March 2026).
- Test set: 58 real canteen tray photos, verified human GT; metric = exact set match per tray (all dishes correct), soft-menu-prefilled prompts, temperature 0, max_tokens 384, client image side 1024 (and native 1920×1080 for the "original" configs).

## Symptom
| stack | set-exact (58) |
|---|---|
| HF transformers (bf16, training-identical stack) | **31** |
| llama.cpp, original image size (no client resize, ~2025 img tokens) | 28 |
| llama.cpp, 1024-side input (~576 tokens), f16 or f32 mmproj, Q8 or bf16 LM, Vulkan or CPU, b10707/b10909/PR#21103-head | **22–24** |
| llama.cpp, image preprocessed to HF-identical 832×448 (~364 tokens) | 16 |

Reproduction is deterministic. Note the monotone pixel-count effect on llama.cpp (352→16, 576→23, 2025→28) — consistent with per-token feature noise being compensated by redundancy.

## Exclusions (all tested)
- **Quantization**: Q4_K_M 19 / Q8_0 23 / bf16 24 — not the driver.
- **Client preprocessing**: feeding HF-processor-identical pixels (832×448 bicubic) makes it worse, not better.
- **Runtime version**: b10707 ≈ b10909 ≈ March base ≈ PR #21103 head (22–24).
- **Backend**: Vulkan 23 ≈ CPU 22 in the same build.
- **mmproj weight precision**: f32 mmproj = f16 mmproj = 23.
- **Chat template / empty-think prefill**: adding the training-time `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` assistant prefill: 21–23, no change.
- **mrope**: sections [24,20,20,0] match HF; LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_IMROPE is selected for QWEN3VL; image position advancement max(nx,ny)=26 matches HF's `max(h,w)//merge`; verified by reading both implementations.
- **Deepstack wiring**: GGUF has `n_deepstack_layers=3`; the 16384-wide input split order [main|ds0|ds1|ds2] verified; injection loop (view at (il+1)*n_embd, added for il<3) reviewed.
- **Vision embedding values**: concat order and per-chunk means/stds match HF to 4 decimal digits.

## Key quantitative evidence (the smoking gun)
Using `MTMD_DEBUG_EMBEDDINGS=1` on the same image (832×448, same pixels both stacks):

- HF *internal* precision floor (same model, f32 vs bf16, vision tower output): `|Δ|mean = 0.0147` (main merger output), 0.0016 / 0.0056 (deepstack outputs).
- HF(bf16) vs mtmd token-0 values: `|Δ| ≈ 0.05–0.15` per element — **≈5× the internal floor** — while global stats (mean/std/min/max/sum over the full [16384×364] tensor) agree to 4 decimal places, i.e. the divergence is zero-mean per-element noise rather than a structural/permutation error.

Conclusion: the mtmd vision path introduces per-element noise ~5× above what the same computation shows internally in HF. Downstream the LLM is sensitive to it (fine-tuned model; accuracy −8/58 @1024), and extra input resolution partially compensates.

## Ask
Please check the vision compute path for precision loss beyond the weights, e.g. f16 intermediate tensors / accumulation order in the vision tower (patch-embed convs, attention, LayerNorm) vs the transformers reference. Happy to run any instrumented build or share the full 58-image benchmark harness/results.

title: Feature request: (server) file upload API
body:
Problem: when user uploads large file, like a long audio recording, the uploading may take a while to finish. If this done on every new message, it will be quite annoying to wait

Proposed solution:
- Add a new POST and GET `files/{id}` API that allow upload (as multipart form data) and check if file exists  
    Note: the GET only return the file metadata, not the actual file; similar to [OAI endpoint](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/files/methods/retrieve)  
    Note (2): for POST, the web ui will be responsible for choosing the file ID, maybe by calculating hash of the file's content
- `/chat/completions` accepts an ID as file, maybe as a specific URI like `file_id://{id}` ; if files doesn't exist, the server returns with a status code error, containing a list of missing files to be uploaded

CC @ggml-org/llama-ui if you agree on the spec to be implemented on the UI

title: Feature Request: WebUI - Projects / Folders for Conversations
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

I've seen it mentioned in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/16938#discussioncomment-16737780 and https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/19223 but I don't think anyone has created an issue yet or at least my searches did not result in anything, so here it is. Pinging @apellaman and @Maykeye as you were interested in this. Also ping @allozaur for feedback.

At the moment, once the WebUI is used for more than quick one-off chats, the chat history can become difficult to navigate. Different conversations often belong to different work contexts, for example in my case:
- coding/debugging
- writing/research
- model testing
- personal stuff
- focused specific projects

A lightweight "Projects" or "Folders" feature would allow users to group related chats together.

The first version could be intentionally simple:
1. Add a project/folder list in the chat sidebar.
2. Allow creating, renaming, and deleting projects/folders.
3. Allow moving conversations into a project/folder.
4. Keep an "Uncategorized" or "Conversations" view for the existing chats without project/folder assignment.
5. Show the current project/folder name in the conversation and/or sidebar.

### Motivation

llama-server is becoming a very good lightweight WebUI for local model use. It is fast, small, easy to run, and does not require a separate stack with a database, accounts, background services, etc.

However, as soon as the WebUI becomes the main interface for day-to-day local LLM use, the number of chats grows quickly. A flat chat list works fine for casual testing, but it becomes harder to use when conversations are part of separate ongoing contexts. Without folders/projects, the user has to rely on conversation titles alone scrolling or searching for the one needed at the moment, or manually clean up old conversations. This adds friction and makes me more likely to reach for another WebUI for more serious usage.

### Possible Implementation

The idea is rather well-explored and widely available in both many commercial and some open source UIs. Below is what I think what definitely needs to be done (maybe in some other form though, I'm not a UI/UX expert), but it's not complete and definitely needs more planning.

1. Update sidebar UI:
```
Projects
  Coding
  Experiments
  Writing
  ...

Conversations
  Write a story about a frog
  Write a story about a fox
  Write a story about a rabbit
  ...
```

2. Add conversation actions:
Move to project...
Remove from project

3. Deleting a project could offer two options:
[ ] Delete chats inside this project
[x] Keep chats and move them to Uncategorized/Conversations list

The safer default should probably be to keep chats and only remove the project assignment.

To avoid making the first implementation too complex, nested folders could be left out initially. A single-level project/folder system is probably enough for a first version.

Optional ideas for the future:
- project/folder-level settings e.g. system prompt
- project/folder-level enabled MCP servers/tools
- search/filter chats within the current project/folder

Those extensions could also interact nicely with the presets idea from #22523, but they are not required for the basic version. The core request is simply: give users a lightweight way to group related chats together.

title: [bug] Built-in tools do not work when llama-server is running in router mode (--models-preset)
body:
### Describe the bug
When running `llama-server` in Router Mode using the `--models-preset` flag, built-in system tools (such as `read_file`, `exec_shell_command`, etc.) visible in the native Web UI dashboard are completely ignored or unusable by the loaded models (tested with Gemma 4 12B and Qwen 3.6 35B MoE).

The tools are correctly populated in the Web UI dropdown upon server startup, but when a model is invoked on-demand by the router, it either hallucinates system tags or politely states it has no local system access (e.g., *"I do not have access to your computer..."*). 

The issue can only be temporarily bypassed by manually writing a hardcoded system prompt inside the Web UI's "System Message" field to force function-calling logic. However, configuring `tools = all` or adding a `system-prompt` string inside the `.ini` file preset crashes the router process entirely (`option not recognized in preset`).

### Reprodution Steps
1. Create a `models.ini` file containing at least one model block configured with tools (e.g., `tools = all`).
2. Start the server via command line using: `llama-server.exe --models-preset models.ini --port 8085 --tools all`
3. Open the native Web UI, select the model, and make sure the built-in tools are checked.
4. Ask the model to perform a local system action (e.g., *"Create a folder on my Desktop named test"*).
5. **Result:** The model completely ignores the available tools and prints a standard text refusal, or gets stuck repeating system/stop tokens.

### Expected Behavior
Models spawned dynamically by the router proxy should inherit the active tool definitions, system templates, and local execution permissions, allowing seamless function-calling just like a single static `llama-server` instance execution.

### Environment Context
- **llama.cpp Build:** b9874
- **Operating System:** Windows 10/11 x64
- **Hardware:** Intel i7-8700k | RTX 5070 (12GB VRAM) | 64GB RAM
- **Backend:** CUDA 13.3 (GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ=1)

title: Feature request: generic layer-window hook - run layers [il_start, il_end) with an injectable/extractable boundary residual
body:
### Prerequisites
- [x] Running latest code (checkout `13f2b28b`).
- [x] Searched open/closed issues (found related #22436, #23568, different ask, see below) and Discussions (#20252 pipeline parallelism).
- [x] This is a new, useful enhancement.

## Feature description

I'd like a small, architecture-agnostic option to run only transformer layers `[il_start, il_end)`. A non-first shard consumes an injected hidden state as the layer-`il_start` input. A non-last shard emits the raw residual entering layer `il_end` instead of logits.

```c
// llama_context_params (or a setter)
int32_t il_start;   // default 0
int32_t il_end;     // default -1 => n_layer
```

I'd want this honored by the shared graph driver, so each arch's builder doesn't have to re-implement it.

## Motivation

I hit this while splitting a model across machines. Cross-machine pipeline (layer) sharding runs a contiguous layer range on each node and passes the boundary residual to the next, so it needs exactly this primitive. It's the building block under the end-user features requested in #22436 (pipeline parallelism over TCP/IP) and #23568 (TP+PP). Today there's no supported way to run a layer subrange starting from an injected residual and read out a boundary residual, so every such effort re-patches the graph builders.

Two of the three pieces already exist and work well:

- Inject. `llama_batch.embd` feeds an external `[n_embd, n_tokens]` residual through `build_inp_embd` (unscaled).
- Per-layer residual capture. `llm_graph_result::t_layer_inp[il]` + `get_layer_inp(il)` and the `embeddings_layer_inp` machinery already record each layer's input hidden state.

The only missing primitive is restricting the layer loop to a range (and, for a boundary shard, skipping the final norm + lm_head and surfacing the layer-`il_end` input residual).

## Supporting evidence: two bugs I found while prototyping this

While implementing a stopgap per-arch patch (below), two issues surfaced that anyone doing partial-graph execution will hit.

1. Embeddings-context defaults to non-causal attention. A context reused to extract a mid-model residual must `llama_set_causal_attn(ctx, true)`, or the residual diverges from the causal model. Easy to miss, worth documenting or defaulting per arch.
2. `inp_out_ids` dangles on a non-final shard. The output-id `get_rows` is keyed on `il == n_layer - 1`. When a shard's last built layer is `< n_layer-1`, `inp_out_ids` is never consumed, and `llm_graph_input_out_ids::set_input` then dereferences its null buffer (`ggml_backend_buffer_is_host(NULL)`, assert). Keying it on the shard's actual last layer fixes it.

I'm happy to open these as separate issues if you'd prefer to track them independently.

## Stopgap I use today

A ~47-line patch adds `il_start/il_end` to `llama_context_params`/`llama_cparams`, loops `[l0,l1)`, keys the `inp_out_ids` `get_rows` on the shard's last layer, and for a boundary shard exposes the pre-norm residual. I verified it bit-exact vs the unsplit model (F32 boundary, CPU and Metal). It's per-arch (`llama.cpp`, `qwen2.cpp`) only because each dense arch has its own builder in `src/models/*.cpp`, which is the reason I'm asking for a generic hook. I'm happy to upstream a generic version.

## Why not RPC / `--split-mode layer`?

Those distribute one logical graph across local devices. They don't give independent per-shard execution with an injectable boundary residual and logits-from-injected-hidden-state, which is what cross-machine pipeline sharding needs.

---
Context: this came up while I was building [Hydra](https://github.com/PavanManchikatla/Hydra), a crash-safe LAN pipeline-inference runtime.

title: Misc. bug: (ggml-hexagon) FLASH_ATTN_EXT produces nondeterministic wrong results on the HMX path (v75/SM8650)
body:
### Name and Version

version: 10297 (6a32c29a7)
built with Clang 18.0.4 for Android aarch64

Hexagon SDK 6.4.0.2, HEXAGON_Tools 19.0.04, NDK r25c
cmake preset: arm64-android-snapdragon-release (GGML_OPENCL=OFF)
Device: Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 / SM8650 / Hexagon v75 (QDC)

### Operating systems

Other? (Please let us know in description)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library), Test code

### Command line

```shell
# reproduce (repo's own adb wrapper)
HB=0 ./scripts/snapdragon/adb/run-tool.sh test-backend-ops -b HTP0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT

# ran it 2-3 times: both the failure count and the failing set change

# narrow it down
HB=0 HMX=0  ./scripts/snapdragon/adb/run-tool.sh test-backend-ops -b HTP0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT   # HMX off  -> 2 failures
HB=0 NHVX=1 ./scripts/snapdragon/adb/run-tool.sh test-backend-ops -b HTP0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT   # 1 thread -> pipelining off

# equivalent, run directly on device
cd /data/local/tmp/llama.cpp
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./lib ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH=./lib GGML_HEXAGON_HOSTBUF=0 \
  ./bin/test-backend-ops -b HTP0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT

Verified against run-tool.sh: HB → GGML_HEXAGON_HOSTBUF, HMX → GGML_HEXAGON_USE_HMX, NHVX → GGML_HEXAGON_NHVX. And the raw form matches what actually executed on the device in job 743551.
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I found a fix for part of the Flash attention causing errors in the numbers when taking HMX path. I traced the issue to a race condition in the HMX queue mechanism. I tested it on qdc :

```
ggml-hex: Hexagon Arch version v75
ggml-hex: HTP0 hwinfo: threads 4, hvx 4, hmx 1, vtcm 8 MB
adb: product:pineapple  model:Pineapple_for_arm64
QDC chipsetAlias: QRD8650
```


### **Dry run of the HMX queue:**
QKn = QK dot for block n. Example QK1 is the QK dot of block 1
OUn = O update for block n. Example OU2 is the O update for block 2


```
ITR 0
  queue: [QK0]    		     # QK0 pushed ahead of loop start
  push QK1          -> [QK0, QK1]
  pop                    -> [QK1]         # got QK0   OK, this is what the code wanted
  (no O update yet, kv_blk == 0)
  (no second pop)
  END OF ITERATION: [QK1] still waiting

ITR 1
  queue: [QK1]
  push QK2        -> [QK1, QK2]
  pop                 -> [QK2]          # got QK1   OK
  push OU0        -> [QK2, OU0]
  softmax
  pop                  -> [OU0]          # got QK2   -- the code believed it waited for OU0
  END OF ITERATION: [OU0] still waiting        <-- an O update leaks into the next iteration

ITR2 2
  queue: [OU0]                                 <-- left over
  push QK3        -> [OU0, QK3]
  pop                -> [QK3]          # got OU0   -- the code believed it waited for QK2
  push OU1        -> [QK3, OU1]
  softmax
  pop             -> [OU1]          # got QK3   -- the code believed it waited for OU1
  END OF ITERATION: [OU1] still waiting

ITR 3   (same shape as iteration 2, forever after)
  queue: [OU1]
  push QK4        -> [OU1, QK4]
  pop                 -> [QK4]          # got OU1
  push OU2        -> [QK4, OU2]
  softmax
  pop                 -> [OU2]          # got QK4
  END OF ITERATION: [OU2] still waiting
```



so from itr2 neither pop waits for what is actually wants. Every update itr ends with an O update still running. 
OU0 reads vtcm_v_tiles[prev_buf] and vtcm_p_tiles[prev_buf]. Its pushed in at itr1 when the buf_idx=1 so prev_buf=0
at step 1 fa_phase_v_interleave(..., vtcm_v_tiles[buf_idx], ...);   // buf_idx == 0
itr2 overwrites v_tiles[0] and its the buffer OU0 is still reading. This is the race condition. 


I did a bunch of testing:
1. Run with GGML_HEXAGON_USE_HMX=0
   102 failures went down to 2. This tell us HMX path is the problem in flash attention.

2. can_pipeline = false hardcoded
   102 failures went down to 32. so the pipeline causes most of them
3. ran same binary twice 
   52 vs 57 failures, different failing sets. 

4. is HMX engine inaccurate? wrote standalone harness in the hexagon sim multiplying matrices with k from 128 to 576 and compared with float32 refs. Matches to the last bit at all depths(found occasional deviations they are negligible). So the athematic is fine

5.  Started testing the queue.
    tried draining the queue before the V interleave across two different jobs two runs each [THE FIX]
    
```
    job         run          unmodified          drain fix
   743500        1            115 fail              49 fail
   743500        2            140 fail              59 fail
   743551        1            112 fail              47 fail
   743551        2            103 fail              53 fail
```


6. Why not just pop once more rather than drain? 
   I tested this first single pop gave 106 and 98 in the back to back runs. 

> Performace cost is +0.1% across 15 cases measured on the same device back to back.

I believe this race condition only caused part of the problem. The fix takes 103-140 down to 47-59, disabling HMX entirely gives 2. The other issue which is causing the errors is still unknown. I have the patch ready its a small change in the beginning of the loop to fix the race.

title: Eval bug: DSpark/DFlash drafter with no_vocab tokenizer ignores tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id → "invalid token = -1" / llama_decode fails
body:
### Name and Version

./llama-server --version
version: 10318 (4cf5cab65)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

Linux m920s 6.8.0-136-generic #136-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Jul  1 21:53:05 UTC 2026 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

- I7-8700T 6C/12T + 128GB DDR4
-  RTX 2000E Ada 16GB

### Models

[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF/tree/main/UD-IQ2_M)
[dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF/resolve/main/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Command line used

```bash
GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1 ./llama-server \
  --model ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/UD-IQ2_M/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --model-draft ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 5 \
  --ctx-size $((64*1024)) \
  --no-context-shift \
  --gpu-layers 999 \
  --n-cpu-moe 43 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 \
  --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --fit off \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --min-k 20 \
  --threads 6 --threads-batch 6 \
  --batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 2048 \
  --cache-ram 0 \
  --jinja \
  --parallel 1 \
  --log-verbosity 4 \
  --no-mmap \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080
```

## Logs

Drafter metadata **does** declare the mask token:

```console
- kv  42:               tokenizer.ggml.model str              = no_vocab
- kv  43:               tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id u32      = 128799
...
print_info: vocab type  = no vocab
```

But the speculative implementation resolves it to -1 and fails on every draft decode:

```console
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: adding speculative implementation 'draft-dspark'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - n_max=5, n_min=0, p_min=0.00
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - block_size=5, mask_token_id=-1, n_extract=3
...
E init: invalid token[1] = -1
E decode: failed to initialize batch
E llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -1
W draft: llama_decode returned -1
(repeats 8x per step, then stalls)
```
## Root cause

**`src/llama-vocab.cpp`** — the `no_vocab` branch sets `special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL` and returns before any metadata is read (~line 1933):

```cpp
if (tokenizer_model == "no_vocab" || tokenizer_model == "none") {
    type = LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_NONE;
    special_bos_id  = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;
    ...
    special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;   // hardcoded; metadata never consulted
    ...
    return;                               // skips the metadata read below
}
```

**`common/speculative.cpp`** (~line 970) trusts the vocab API with no fallback:

```cpp
mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));   // returns -1
```

That `-1` is then injected into the draft batch (~line 1153):

```cpp
common_batch_add(batch, i == 0 ? dp.id_last : mask_token_id, n + i, { seq_id }, true);
```

→ `invalid token[1] = -1` → `llama_decode` returns -1.

The metadata key is valid and correctly mapped in `src/llama-arch.cpp:345`:

```cpp
{ LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id" },
```

It's simply unreachable on the `no_vocab` path.

## Suggested fix

`common/speculative.cpp` already reads another drafter field (`dflash.block_size`) directly from metadata via `llama_model_meta_val_str` for exactly this reason (~line 962). Applying the same pattern to the mask token is the smallest, most contained fix:

```diff
         mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));
+
+        // no_vocab drafters (DSpark/DFlash) nullify the mask token in the vocab, so
+        // fall back to the GGUF metadata key when the vocab API returns nothing.
+        // Mirrors the dflash.block_size metadata read above.
+        if (mask_token_id < 0) {
+            char buf[32] = {};
+            if (llama_model_meta_val_str(model_dft, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id", buf, sizeof(buf)) >= 0) {
+                mask_token_id = (llama_token) std::atoi(buf);
+            }
+        }
```

With this change, the log line flips from `mask_token_id=-1` to `mask_token_id=128799` and the `invalid token` / decode failures stop. No new includes needed — `llama_model_meta_val_str` and `std::atoi` are already used a few lines above for `dflash.block_size`.

(An alternative, broader fix would be to read `LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID` inside the `no_vocab` branch of `src/llama-vocab.cpp` so `llama_vocab_mask()` returns the right value for any caller — but the change above is sufficient for the speculative path and carries no risk to other vocab consumers.)

title: qwen35: TENSOR_SKIP on MTP block triggers "unused tensor" warnings for regular attention/FFN weights
body:
### Name and Version

version: 10327 (69bf64379)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Intel i5-13600K + Nvidia 3090

### Models

bartowski/Qwen_Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF:Q3_K_M

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I don't think any of the parameters cause this, but this are my current parameters:
./llama-server.exe -hf bartowski/Qwen_Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF:Q3_K_M --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 -ngl -1 -c 229376 -b 2048 -ub 2048 --cache-prompt -fa on --cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 --temp 0.6 --top_k 20 --repeat_penalty 1.05 --jinja --no-skip-chat-parsing --reasoning-format deepseek --reasoning-preserve --parallel 2 --kv-unified
This will throw the error on the logs below.

After a conversation with my agent, this is what we concluded:
- Commit 82dbc4f ("load MTP tensors only if they are really used", Jul 31) introduced the regression
- Line 42 of src/models/qwen35.cpp: int mtp_flags = !ml.load_mtp ? TENSOR_SKIP : 0;
- This applies TENSOR_SKIP to ALL blk.64 tensors (attn_norm, attn_qkv, wo, ffn_gate/down/up) when MTP is disabled
- TENSOR_SKIP triggers the "unused tensor" warning at llama-model-loader.cpp:1118
- For Qwen3.6-27B (block_count=65, n_layer_nextn=1), blk.64 is a hybrid MTP block with both attention/FFN and nextn tensors — the attention/FFN tensors shouldn't be skipped, only the nextn-specific ones
- The fix: apply mtp_flags (with TENSOR_SKIP) only to nextn-specific tensors in load_block_mtp, not to attention/FFN tensors

### First Bad Commit

I'm not sure when started as I've not updated my local llama.cpp in a about a month, but my agent did a search and identified this commit as a possible cause:  Commit 82dbc4f ("load MTP tensors only if they are really used", Jul 31) introduced the regression

title: Feature Request: CUDA graphs for multi-slot decode via shape-stable padded u
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Decouple graph shapes from the number of *active* slots: always prepare decode ubatches
padded to a fixed number of token positions B (B = `n_parallel`, or a small bucket set
{1,2,4,8}):

- inactive positions get a dummy token id;
- attention mask: padding **key** columns are −inf for all queries; padding **query** rows
  produce outputs that are never consumed (logit consumption reads only real slots);
- KV cache: padding K/V is written to a reserved dummy row (unified/ring KV), so real
  entries are never overwritten;
- `out_ids` fixed; content changes per step, shapes do not.

Then galloc reserves once, cgraph captures once per bucket, and steady state is
`set_inputs` + `cudaGraphLaunch`. Prefill stays unpadded: it is compute-bound, a separate
graph family, and rebuilding there is amortized by arithmetic.

This implies relaxing the batch>1 cgraph disable for shape-stable graphs: the restriction
exists because the update/patch path cannot track structural changes — with padding there
is nothing to track.

### Motivation

The practical consequence: `llama-server --parallel N` loses CUDA graphs entirely as soon
as ≥2 slots decode together. Every step falls back to the full pipeline: graph build,
`ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph`, per-kernel `cudaLaunchKernel`, input copies, sync. I have CPU
profiles showing exactly this: with 1 active slot the step is a cgraph replay; with 2
active slots every step is build+alloc+launch. Repro: run server with `-np 2`, send two
concurrent decodes, observe the disable message and per-step launch overhead in a profile.

Decode is the latency-critical steady state, and at small batches launch overhead is a
large fraction of step time — i.e. multi-slot serving pays exactly the tax cgraph was
built to remove.

### Cost model

Decode is memory-bandwidth bound: weights are streamed once per step regardless of
n_tokens. Padding 1→B active tokens adds negligible compute and trades it for removing
all launch/allocation overhead.

### Prior art

- vLLM: CUDA graph cache keyed by (padded) batch — core design.
- TensorRT-LLM: CUDA graph padding (e.g. "MTP with CUDA graph padding" in release notes).
- NVIDIA CUDA Graph best practices: "Solution 1 — Padding to fixed size".
- SGLang: fixed-batch capture for decode.

### Related

- #6763 (original cgraph integration), #7302 (avoid unnecessary cgraph disabling);
- #16548 (cgraph plans for split graphs — complementary: padding keeps shapes stable so
  reuse heuristics trivially hit);
- #20315, #25082 (cgraph cache growth from per-step shape/offset changes — padding
  collapses the cache key space and mitigates both);
- #3479 (batched decode performance), #11614 (cgraph disabled at batch > 1).

### Open questions

- Flash attention: with an explicit `kq_mask`, −inf columns suffice; with FA, padding keys
  need out-of-window positions or a kernel-side ignore flag. Which path first?
- B = `n_parallel` vs bucketing (capture count vs wasted compute).
- SWA models: ring size is already constant, so `n_kv` dim is stable; mask is window×B.
- Interaction with speculative decoding / MTP (per-layer residual outputs).

```cpp
// tools/server/server-http.cpp

    sink.done(); // <-- crash site

The "obvious" fix is to check if `sink` is valid before calling `done()`:

```patch
From 33193ef095fbbc661fb6bf4225b9900628c41ed0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eugene Palmoff <mahou@shoujo.pw>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 19:44:05 +0500
Subject: [PATCH] Fix unchecked call to sink.done()

---
 tools/server/server-http.cpp | 4 +++-
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/tools/server/server-http.cpp b/tools/server/server-http.cpp
index b11dc09d0..449a141eb 100644
--- a/tools/server/server-http.cpp
+++ b/tools/server/server-http.cpp
@@ -565,7 +565,9 @@ static void process_handler_response(server_http_req_ptr && request, server_http
                 SRV_DBG("http: streamed chunk: %s\n", chunk.c_str());
             }
             if (!has_next) {
-                sink.done();
+                if (sink.done) {
+                    sink.done();
+                }
                 SRV_DBG("%s", "http: stream ended\n");
             }
             return has_next;
-- 
2.53.0

```

After applying the patch, I was able to run the server for a few hours without any crashes. That said, I have no idea what I'm doing here, which is why this is a bug report and not a PR.

No idea. I've been observing these crashes for the past month, at the very least. The bug is too difficult to reproduce reliably to identify the exact commit.

title: Misc. bug: -no-cnv has no effect on llama-cli; the process then blocks at ">" forever
body:
## Name and Version

```
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10453, commit 3cb7ffb1a)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
```

Also reproduced on `b10448` (`ad1de39e0`).

## Operating systems

Windows

## Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-cli

## Command line

```
llama-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ngl 99 -c 4096 -n 32 -no-cnv --no-warmup -p "1+1="
```

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

`-no-cnv` / `--no-conversation` is listed in `llama-cli --help` and documented in `tools/cli/README.md` as disabling conversation mode. On the new `llama-cli` it has no effect: conversation mode starts regardless, the prompt is consumed as the first user turn, and after generating the answer the process blocks at `>` waiting for input until it is killed.

Steps:

1. Run the command above.
2. Observe the banner, the `/exit /regen /clear` command list, and `> 1+1=` — i.e. conversation mode, despite `-no-cnv`.
3. The answer is generated and the perf line is printed.
4. The process never exits.

Controls — same machine, same model, only the marked change:

| change | result |
|---|---|
| as above | never exits (killed at 150 s) |
| `-st` instead of `-no-cnv` | exits cleanly, code 0, 14.6 s |
| `llama-completion`, same args including `-no-cnv` | exits cleanly, code 0, 14.2 s |
| stdin redirected from an empty file | exits on its own, code 130 |

The `-st` row isolates the flag: same binary, same model, same environment, only `-no-cnv` → `-st` changes, and the process exits in 14.6 s. The stdin-EOF row shows the process is genuinely blocked on console input rather than looping.

This is not tty-dependent — the result is identical with stdout redirected to a file and with a real console attached — and it is not new in `b10453`; `b10448` behaves the same way.

Either the flag should do what it says, or it should be removed from `llama-cli --help` and from `tools/cli/README.md`. As it stands it is accepted silently and does nothing, which sends scripted and non-interactive callers into what looks like an unexplained hang: no output, no error, no exit code. `-st` works, and `llama-completion` is the documented path for deterministic pipelines (#17618), but nothing at the point of use points there.

Possibly related: #18200 proposes disabling conversation mode when stdin or stdout is not a tty, which would also have avoided this in the scripted case.

On scope: I have only tested on Windows. Nothing in the observed behaviour looks platform-specific — the flag simply does not disable conversation mode — but I have not verified on Linux or macOS and would be happy to if that helps. My guess as to why this seems under-reported is that it only bites when `llama-cli` is driven non-interactively (scripts, CI, coding agents). Interactive users never pass `-no-cnv`, and a blocked non-interactive process emits nothing to diagnose, so it tends to be misattributed to whatever is driving it.

## Relevant log output

```
build      : b10453-3cb7ffb1a
model      : Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
ftype      : Q4_K - Small
modalities : text

available commands:
  /exit or Ctrl+C     stop or exit
  /regen              regenerate the last response
  /clear              clear the chat history
  /read <file>        add a text file
  /glob <pattern>     add text files using globbing pattern


> 1+1=

[Start thinking]

The user is asking a simple math question: 1+1=?

The answer is 2.

This is straightforward. No need for elaborate reasoning.

[ Prompt: 206.8 t/s | Generation: 33.4 t/s ]

>
```

(process still alive here; killed at 150 s)

title: Compile bug: Level Zero loader or headers not found, Level Zero support disabled
body:
### Git commit

$git rev-parse HEAD
d83f72d463287ab9c50b4bc18ee332104a963889


### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

SYCL

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I am trying to compile llama.cpp with SYCL backend on a laptop running the latest OpenSuse Slowroll. Compiling completes successfully, but for some reason "level zero" support gets disabled ("Level Zero loader or headers not found, Level Zero support disabled"), although it seems to be there and my single integrated intel GPU is seems to be correctly recognized as such, see below.
Is this a bug or am I missing something to get level zero to work?

$ source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh

   args: Using "$@" for setvars.sh arguments:

title: server: deadlock under sustained chat workload on Gemma 4 26B-A4B + Vulkan (regression between v194 and v0.2.0-dev)
body:
**last known good:** v194 (69bf643) — 24h+ soak clean
**first known bad:** 0.2.0-dev build 433 (bb4caa754)

## Symptom

llama-server deadlocks after serving several hundred sequential chat requests. The log stops mid-request at a `slot get_availabl` line; no further activity for minutes until the client times out and the server logs `srv stop: cancel task`. After that the server is fully wedged: `/health` does not respond, new requests are not even logged, but the process stays alive. No errors or warnings in the log around the stall, no GPU driver faults in dmesg, GTT memory usage normal (21.9/48 GiB). Decode throughput degrades noticeably before the stall (~74 -> ~62 t/s on the last tasks).

## Repro

- Model: `unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF` QAT UD-Q4_K_XL (~13.3 GiB)
- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo APU (Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, Radeon 8060S iGPU, gfx1151, unified memory), Mesa RADV 26.0.3, kernel 7.0
- Launch flags: `-ngl 99 --load-mode mlock --ctx-size 262144 --kv-unified --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --flash-attn on --jinja --reasoning on --reasoning-format auto -b 2048 -ub 512 -t 16 -tb 16 -np 4` (env `GGML_VK_DISABLE_MMVQ=1`)
- Workload: sequential OpenAI-compatible chat completions with tool definitions, shared long system prompt (heavy prefix reuse across slots), temp 1.0, several hundred requests. Stall reproduced twice: after ~1300 and after ~650 tasks.

The same workload on the same machine/driver with v194 (69bf643) runs indefinitely without issue. A bisect over the ~600 commits between 69bf643 and bb4caa754 was not performed.

## Log tail at stall

```
16.59.676.681 I slot print_timing: id  2 | task 1289 |    graphs reused =       1172
16.59.678.255 I slot      release: id  2 | task 1289 | stop processing: n_tokens = 1645, truncated = 0
16.59.705.927 I slot get_availabl: id  2 | task -1 | selected slot by LCP similarity, f_sim_best = 0.384 (> 0.100 thold), f_keep = 0.364
21.48.316.033 W srv          stop: cancel task, id_task = 1295
```

Happy to run a bisect or test a debug build if you point me at a suspect area (slot management / kv-unified / unified KV cache path changed a lot in this window).

title: HIP/gfx1151: SOLVE_TRI aborts with rocBLAS 'hipErrorInvalidImage' (device kernel image is invalid)
body:
### Summary

On **gfx1151 (Strix Halo, Windows 11)** the HIP backend crashes in `GGML_OP_SOLVE_TRI` with a rocBLAS kernel-image error. Reproducible via `test-backend-ops`; it also makes any graph that contains SOLVE_TRI (e.g. the **unfused gated-delta-net path**, relevant for Qwen3.5/Kimi-linear when the fused kernels are disabled) unusable on this platform.

### Environment

- HW: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S iGPU (**gfx1151**), Windows 11 Pro 26200, Adrenalin 32.0.31035.1003
- ROCm runtime: TheRock `therock-dist-windows-gfx1151-7.14.0rc3` (rocblas.dll + bundled `rocblas/library` Tensile kernels from the same tarball)
- llama.cpp: b10582 (e85caa81e), self-built with the TheRock clang toolchain, `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151`

### Reproduction

```
test-backend-ops test -o SOLVE_TRI
```

Output (after 6 passing cases):

```
  SOLVE_TRI(type=f32,ne_lhs=[64,64,2,2],ne_rhs=[10,64,2,2]): OK
  ...
rocBLAS error from hip error code: 'hipErrorInvalidImage':200
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: SOLVE_TRI failed
ROCm error: device kernel image is invalid
  current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_compute_forward at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:2408
ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:106: ROCm error
```

The hard abort also kills a full `test-backend-ops test` run at this point, so op coverage after SOLVE_TRI is not reachable on this platform without `-o` filtering.

Same behavior when running a model graph that reaches SOLVE_TRI (unfused gated-delta-net path via disabled fused kernels), including with `ROCBLAS_TENSILE_LIBPATH` explicitly pointed at the tarball's `rocblas/library`.

Possibly related to the class of #19880 (`hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction` on gfx906), but different error code, arch and entry point — filing separately as requested there.

### Ask

Is the rocBLAS/Tensile solve path expected to be supported on gfx1151, or should `supports_op` exclude SOLVE_TRI on this arch (CPU fallback) until it is? Happy to test patches — deterministic repro, ~3 s.

title: Feature Request: Show Model Info dialog for unloaded models in Router Mode
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Since https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/20600, we have a model information dialog available in router mode. While it contains slightly less information than the dialog in non-router mode, it is still highly useful.

**Current Behavior:**
The model information icon/button to open this dialog is currently only available for models that are *already loaded* in the router.



### Motivation

**Observation / Technical Context:**
While looking into the code (I actually started drafting a PR for this myself before #20600 was merged by @ServeurpersoCom), I noticed that the underlying dialog implementation is already pretty robust. It gracefully handles missing information by simply omitting those fields from the UI, without throwing errors or crashing.

In fact, if you simply bypass or remove the check that restricts the info button to loaded models, almost all the static model information is already available and renders perfectly in the dialog. The necessary code to fetch and display this metadata is already present under the hood. No new backend logic or complex GGUF header parsing seems to be required.

### Possible Implementation

**Proposed Behavior:**
Make the model info button available for **all** models listed in the router preset, regardless of their loaded state. Implementation-wise, this likely just means removing the `is_loaded` (or similar) condition that currently hides the button for unloaded models in the router UI.

**UI Suggestion:**
To avoid user confusion regarding the missing runtime-specific information (like current KV cache usage, active slot states, etc., which naturally only exist when loaded), a subtle note or banner could be added to the top of the dialog when viewing an unloaded model. For example:
> *"Model not currently loaded. Some runtime information may be unavailable."*

This would be a very low-effort "quick win" that greatly improves the UX. It allows users to inspect a model's specifications before deciding to load it.

title: Feature Request: Model navigation and load controls in Router Model Info dialog (Follow-up to #27563)
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

I propose adding a navigation and control bar to the Model Information dialog in Router Mode. This bar would provide the following controls:

1. Previous (`<`) / Next (`>`) buttons: To cycle through the models defined in the current router preset.
2. Status indicator: A simple text label showing whether the currently viewed model is `loaded` or `not loaded`.
3. Load / Unload button: Allows the user to load or unload the currently displayed model directly from the dialog.

### Motivation

When working with a large `router-preset.ini`, inspecting multiple models currently requires a repetitive workflow: open model info -> close dialog -> find the next model in the main list -> open model info again. 

If a user wants to compare the specifications of several models (e.g., all quantizations of a specific family, or all models matching a certain search term), this becomes quite tedious. This feature would allow users to inspect, compare, and selectively load models in one continuous workflow without constantly closing and reopening the dialog.

Combined with #27563 (which suggests showing model info for unloaded models), this would act as a powerful "model browser". It greatly improves model management by allowing users to comfortably step through and check a model's static specs *before* deciding to actually load it into memory.

### Possible Implementation

- Navigation Logic: The `<` and `>` buttons would step through the internal list of models loaded from the preset. Ideally, this navigation respects the current filter state of the "search models" box in the main Router UI. This way, a user can type a search term and then use the arrows to step only through the matching models.
- State Management: The dialog would need to listen to the router's model state to accurately display the `loaded` / `not loaded` indicator and toggle the Load/Unload button text/action accordingly.
- Action Binding: The Load/Unload button would trigger the same backend API calls that are currently used when loading/unloading a model from the main model list UI.
- UI Placement: The control bar could be placed either at the top or the bottom of the existing Model Info dialog layout.

This builds directly on top of the Model Info dialog introduced in #20600 and the proposed enhancements in #27563.

title: Eval bug: probabilistic CUDA error 'invalid argument' at kernel launch on 7x Volta (sm_70) layer-split, triggered by large prefill + partial prefix reuse
body:
### Name and Version

Running llama.cpp through LM Studio runtime packs, b10760 through b11026 (runtime 2.31.2 - 2.41.0). All of them crash for me. I have Windows Error Reporting records pinning each crash to the exact engine binary via PE timestamp, so this is not a stale-process artifact.

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

7x Volta sm_70 (1x Quadro GV100 + 6x Tesla PG503-216, 32 GB HBM2 each), `--split-mode layer --tensor-split 0 --main-gpu 0`, CUDA graphs disabled via `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`.

### Models

Reproduces across architectures (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF and DeepSeek-V4-Flash variants, various quantizations), so I don't think it's model-specific. UBatches 256 and 384 both crash at the same rate on the Qwen model.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

During normal long agent sessions (OpenAI-compatible server, one client, very long contexts with heavy prefix reuse) llama-server dies roughly daily — recently ~6 times a day — with a fail-fast (`0xc0000409` in ucrtbase.dll). The last engine line before death is always:

```
CUDA error: invalid argument
current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_kernel_launch at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh:<line varies by build: 1676/1710/1716>
```

The trigger pattern is consistent across three weeks of logs (~100 crashes): a large prefill (tens of thousands of tokens, up to ~112K context) with high partial prefix-cache reuse (`f_keep` 0.98-0.99), dying either right at the prefill→decode boundary (`progress = 1.00`) or mid-prefill around a batch boundary. It is probabilistic: replaying the same session mostly works, and a synthetic append-only stress run (growing prefix, ~3K new tokens per round) passed 40/40 rounds once and crashed in round 2 another time. Note it does NOT strictly require >100K context — I also have samples at 56K, 18K, and even a fresh slot crashing on its first 2-message prefill; deep context just raises the probability.

What I've ruled out by testing, not guessing:
- Engine version. Clean reinstall of runtime 2.33 still crashes (~1/day); 2.34 through 2.41 crash more often (6-10/day). #28177 and #28198 (merged Sep 3/4) look like amplifiers on the multi-GPU launch path, not the root cause.
- KV quantization (`q8_0` K/V): survived 9.5h / ~200K new prefill tokens once, then reproduced the exact same signature. Reduces frequency at best.
- `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`: verified present in the process PEB environment. Helps on ≤2.33 builds; newer builds have launch paths that bypass it and crash anyway.
- `--no-kv-unified`, split strategy (spread vs priority-order fill): no effect.

Since both `cudaLaunchKernelEx` and the classic launch path reject the same configuration, I suspect a grid/block dimension goes out of range for some batch shape on sm_70 — similar in spirit to #27901 (gridDim.y overflow), but here it seems to need multi-GPU layer split plus partial slot reuse to show up. Volta is presumably not covered by any CI runner, which might be why this survives.

I could not reduce this to a clean `llama-completion` repro yet because the failure needs the prefix-cache reuse pattern of a long agent session; I'm happy to run bisects or test patches against my workload — I have crash logs with exact timestamps, token counts and f_keep values for every occurrence. Related but distinct signatures: #28661 (fattn-mma-f16.cuh:1945, non-standard head dim), #27871/#27901 (GB10 gridDim.y).

**First bad commit:** unknown — every runtime from b10760 to b11026 crashes; the frequency jump around Sep 3/4 suggests #28177 / #28198 amplified an older bug rather than introducing it.

title: Feature: Improve Message Steering & Queuing features
UI Bug: Editing assistant message duplicates reasoning block and corrupts stored content
body:
When editing a model's response in Web UI that contains a reasoning block, the reasoning gets duplicated and a new copy is encased in `<think></think>` tags. This is recent new behaviour (I updated yesterday after about a week) and it seems unintended. Before, reasoning was non-editable at all, so it seems part of the idea was to expose it to editing.

I asked the DeepWiki bot to summarise and identify the cause. It found the (probable) affected files, but couldn't trace which commit introduced the change, since the files were apparently reorganised recently.

The following summary was written by the DeepWiki bot. It also suggested to tag @allozaur

(Sorry if this report is not up to par. I can only use GitHub with a phone app atm.)

---

**Description**

When editing an assistant message that contains a reasoning/thinking block, the reasoning content is duplicated in the display and the stored message is corrupted.

**Steps to reproduce (Web UI)**
1. Use a reasoning model (e.g. Gemma 4 E4b)
2. Ask a question and receive a response that includes a thinking block
3. Click Edit on the assistant message
4. Save the edit (with or without changes)

**Expected behavior**
The reasoning block is editable and saved correctly, with no duplication.

**Actual behavior**
- In edit mode, the reasoning appears twice: once as the collapsible "Reasoning" block (rendered from `reasoningContent`), and again as `<think>...</think>` literal text in the textarea.
- After saving, `content` contains `<think>...</think>` as embedded literal text, while `reasoningContent` retains the original unchanged value. This causes the duplication to persist in the rendered view.
- When the next message is generated, the corrupted message is sent to the backend as context, with both `reasoning_content` and `<think>` tags in `content`.

**Root cause**

`rawEditContent` in `ChatMessage.svelte` (lines 48–90) reconstructs the full message for the edit textarea, wrapping reasoning in `<think>...</think>` tags. However, `editAssistantMessage` in `chat.svelte.ts` only writes the edited text to `content` and never updates or clears `reasoningContent`. The `shouldBranch` path has the same issue — it creates a new message with `content: newContent` but no `reasoningContent` field at all.

Relevant files:
- `tools/ui/src/lib/components/app/chat/ChatMessages/ChatMessage/ChatMessage.svelte` — `rawEditContent` construction (lines 48–90)
- `tools/ui/src/lib/stores/chat.svelte.ts` — `editAssistantMessage` save paths (lines 1445–1463)

**Additional notes**

The `REASONING_TAGS` are hardcoded as `<think>`/`</think>` regardless of model. The codebase already deprecated embedding reasoning tags in `content` in favor of a dedicated `reasoningContent` field (`LEGACY_REASONING_TAGS`). The current approach re-introduces the same anti-pattern.

A correct fix would require `editAssistantMessage` to parse `<think>...</think>` out of the edited content, store the extracted text in `reasoningContent`, and store only the remaining text in `content`. Alternatively, reasoning could be exposed as a separate editable field in the UI rather than serialized into the textarea.

body:
It would be very useful to expose custom runtime parameters directly in the web GUI.

Currently, some parameters (for example enabling/disabling "think mode") can only be changed through CLI arguments or API configuration, but there is no simple way to modify them from the web interface.

### Requested Feature

Add a generic GUI section for custom parameters / advanced flags, allowing users to:

* enable or disable boolean options
* edit custom inference parameters
* dynamically change runtime flags without restarting or editing configs manually

Example:

* `think mode`: ON / OFF

### Why This Helps

This would improve usability for non-technical users and make experimentation much easier directly from the web UI.

It could also make future custom parameters automatically available without requiring dedicated GUI updates for each one.

title: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid Gated DeltaNet): decode throughput collapses ~25x at context positions >~80K while prompt processing stays fast
body:
## Environment

- **llama.cpp**: master `8144f31` (2026-08-23) + also reproduced on release b10488 (Windows CUDA 13.3 build)
- **OS**: Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (both tested, same cliff)
- **GPU**: RTX 4080 SUPER 16GB, driver 591.86 (CUDA 13.1), nvcc 13.1, sm_89
- **Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2GB); also reproduced with UD-IQ4_XS (13.3GB) and IQ4_XS (14.6GB)
- **Backend**: CUDA, single GPU

## Symptom

With the model **fully resident on GPU** (zero "assigned to device CPU" lines, verified in logs), decode (tg) speed collapses non-linearly once the KV position exceeds roughly 80K tokens — from ~33 t/s at 68K position to **1.4 t/s (714 ms/token) at 91K position**, or outright timeouts. **Prompt processing (pp) stays fast (~1300 t/s) at the same positions.** Zero-context decode is normal (~38-39 t/s) on every configuration below.

## Reproduction matrix (WSL2, llama-server)

Command shape:
```
./llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 999 --load-mode none \
    -c <CTX> [-fa on] -ctk <Q> -ctv <Q>
```
Then send a chat completion with a ~91K-token filler prompt and `max_tokens=100`.

| Config | VRAM fit (CPU overrides) | pp @91K fill | tg @91K position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits, 0 CPU lines | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` | fits | fast | **timed out (>25 min)** |
| `-c 98304  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **timed out** |
| `-c 73728  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **33.1 t/s @ 68K position ✅** |

Position sweep with the last config (UD-Q3_K_XL, q8 KV, no FA):

| KV position (prompt tokens) | decode t/s (server-side timing) |
|---|---|
| 45,574 | 35.6 |
| 60,309 | 33.9 |
| 68,642 | 33.1 |
| 91,077 | **1.4 (or timeout)** |

## Key observations

1. **The cliff is positional, not a memory-spill issue.** All 96K/128K configs above report 0 CPU tensor overrides and normal free VRAM headroom; KV quantization level (q4/q5/q8) and `-fa on/off` make no difference to the cliff. Only the *position* matters.
2. **pp is unaffected at the same positions** (~1300 t/s for the 91K fill), so this is specific to the decode path.
3. The drop is far steeper than any plausible O(n) attention-scan cost: 68K→91K position is a 1.34x context increase but a **~24x decode slowdown**.
4. Server logs at the cliff show `eval time = 1055.41 ms / 300 tokens (0.95 tokens per second)` with `graphs reused = 298`, i.e. CUDA graph reuse continues normally while per-token latency explodes.
5. Also reproduced on the same hardware under Windows native (b10488) at large `-c`, so it is not WSL2-specific.

## Suspected area

Decode-path attention over long KV for the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers (Qwen3.8 / qwen35-family). Possibly a fallback/slow kernel engaged past some KV extent threshold. Possibly related family: #27442 (empty generation >16K on Metal for qwen35moe hybrids), #27572 (draft acceptance collapse with multi-ubatch batches).

## Logs

Full `llama-server` logs for the 131072/q4/FA and 73728/q8/no-FA runs available on request (happy to attach — they contain per-token timing lines, tensor placement, and KV buffer sizes).

title: Misc. bug: OpenVINO GPU code paths are silently disabled on GPU.N machines, causing wrong results and performance drops
body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11003, commit 37b53fd45)
built with Clang 24.0.0 for Linux x86_64
OS: Linux Mint 22.3, kernel 6.18.17
OpenVINO: 2026.5.0
GPU: Intel Arc Pro B70 (dGPU) + Intel UHD Graphics 770 (iGPU)
Level Zero driver: 1.17.0

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Overview
On a Multi-GPU machine OpenVINO enumerates devices as GPU.0, GPU.1, ... At the same time in llama.cpp OpenVINO backend there are ~20 places that compare device name with "GPU" string (see: `git grep "== \"GPU\""`).  

There are two sets of consequences depending on how user configures `GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE` - both are bad. Both exist from the very beginning of this backend.

### GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU
When user sets `GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU`, then computations go to CPU, see message `GGML OpenVINO Backend: device GPU is not available, fallback to CPU`. GPU is unused.

### GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU.N
When user sets `GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU.0` (or GPU.1 ...), then comparison with "GPU" gives *false*.  Model executes on GPU as expected (because `ov::Core::get_available_devices()` returns name with dot and that name is found by llama.cpp), but...
- some operations fail or give incorrect results because they execute on GPU while they should be routed to CPU as known limitations
- KV cache is kept on the host instead of device, and ...
- a manual, fast, GQN attention is never used on GPU.N in [ggml/src/ggml-openvino/openvino/op/flash_attn_ext.cpp#L130](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/e6cef8152f6e8351a870d8e1a98627139c9c379a/ggml/src/ggml-openvino/openvino/op/flash_attn_ext.cpp#L130) so ...
- performance for large context can drop significantly

## Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure you have an llama.cpp tag without recent blocker issue in OpenVINO exposed by https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28549 where prompt above 512 tokens fails with `res = -3`.
2. Ensure your machine uses multiple indexed GPU devices:
```
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU.0 llama-bench --list-devices 2>&1 | grep "OpenVINO: using"
```
output:
```
OpenVINO: using device GPU.0
```
3. See that setting device to just "GPU" fallbacks to CPU
```
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU llama-bench --list-devices 2>&1 | grep OpenVINO
```
output:
```
GGML OpenVINO Backend: device GPU is not available, fallback to CPU
OpenVINO: using device CPU
  OPENVINO0: OpenVINO Runtime (64030 MiB, 64030 MiB free)
```
4. See correctness failures due to not routing operations to CPU. e.g. by
```
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU.1 test-backend-ops test -b OPENVINO0 -o MUL_MAT_ID -p "type_a=f16,"
```
Results observed: 90 out of 92 cases fails, 2 not supported, 0 passes, `MUL_MAT_ID` throws `ov::Exception` and gives huge error `[MUL_MAT_ID] ERR = 81.610077935 > 0.000500000`.
 
5. See performance drop in decode phase (tested on B70). In large contexts performance of decode phase on the same backend and on the same device is significantly lower if only used under name with dot (GPU.N instead of GPU, that is when other GPU is not masked). Please note to use proper mask, valid on your machine, when reproducing.
```
A="-m $HOME/models/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf -ngl 999 -p 512 -n 128 -d 128,4096 -r 3"
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU.1                   llama-bench --device OPENVINO0 $A
ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0 GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=GPU  llama-bench --device OPENVINO0 $A
```

The table below summarizes results (tok/s, Intel Arc Pro B70, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M model)
| configuration | tg128 @ d128 | tg128 @ d4096 | pp512 @ d128 | pp512 @ d4096 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenVINO, Arc as GPU.1 | 44.1 | **9.6** (4.3x slow down) | 5437.3 | 2388.4 |
| OpenVINO, Arc as GPU | 59.7 | 41.1 | 5337.8 | 3043.0 |


## Related issues

- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22644 - unsuccessful attempt to make Multi-GPU working with OpenVINO (as author says *This change has not made OpenVINO useful for me*)
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25562 - unsuccessful attempt to make Multi-GPU docker work with OpenVINO 

### First Bad Commit

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/9789c4ecdc01d571331c14e5197514b53839de4b
ggml : add OpenVINO backend (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/15307)
2026-03-14

### Relevant log output
